item.title: Immigration sets 5 targets for new Comptrollers, as IGP seeks stronger partnership
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Comptroller General of the Nigeria Immigration Service NIS, Kemi Nandap, has set five “non-negotiable” expectations for newly promoted Comptrollers, ordering them to lead by example, deliver measurable results, protect the Service’s integrity, embrace reforms and develop their personnel. The Inspector General of Police IGP, Olatunji Disu, also pledged the Nigeria Police Force’s commitment to a stronger partnership with the Service. Both spoke on Thursday at the decoration of 94 new Comptrollers of Immigration. A total of 106 officers were promoted, but 12 retired before the ceremony. Nandap told the officers that their new rank came with heavier demands. “Promotion is not simply a reward for what you have accomplished. It is a declaration of confidence in what you are now expected to do,” she said. She said the rank was “a greater burden of trust” and a higher standard of conduct. “I have some expectations of you, and they are non-negotiable. First, you must lead by example. Two, you must deliver measurable results. Thirdly, protect the integrity of the service. Fourth, embrace innovation and institutional reforms. Change starts with you. Your attitude matters. And lastly, number five, develop your people. You must build competent and motivated and disciplined teams that are capable of sustaining progress of the service”, she demanded. The Comptroller General said the expectations were not ceremonial. “They are practical standards against which your leadership should be assessed. And I urge you to personally hold yourself accountable,” she said. She told the officers that the Service needed more than senior officers. It needs more effective leaders, Nandap said. “Corruption, extortion, abuse of office, professional negligence, and indiscipline have no place in the Nigerian immigration service we have built here. I expect every controller to demonstrate zero tolerance for misconduct. You cannot demand integrity from your subordinates while compromising your own principles”, she added. According to her, ongoing reforms were meant to make the Service professional, intelligence-led and technologically enabled. She cited the e-Border Solution, the Border Control and Immigration Management System (BCIMS) and the e-Gates among the digital platforms being deployed. But she cautioned that technology alone would not deliver results. “Our technology, no matter how sophisticated, cannot compensate for weak leadership, poor information, indiscipline, or the lack of accountability,” she said. She told the Comptrollers to ensure the reforms reached commands, border posts and airports. “You must take ownership of the systems entrusted to your formations. You must ensure that officers are properly trained,” she said. item.title: McIlroy makes strong start in bid to equal Montgomerie's record
item.description: McIlroy is chasing a fifth successive Race to Dubai triumph this week [Getty Images] DP World Tour Championship first-round leaderboard -5 J Luiten (Ned); -4 JS Olesen (Den); -3 V Perez (Fra), G De Leo (Ita), F Schott (Ger), F Laporta (Ita), R McIlroy (NI) Selected others: -2 T Hatton (Eng); -1 D Hillier (NZ), J Rahm (Spa); E E Chacarra (Spa), M Wallace (Eng); +2 E Ferguson (Sco), R Fox (NZ), C Jarvis (SA), J Schaper (SA); +3 P Reed (US); +4 T Fleetwood (Eng), A Rai (Eng) Full leaderboard Rory McIlroy made a strong start to his bid for a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title with a three-under-par opening round at the DP World Tour Championship. The world number two, whose round included five birdies and two bogeys in windy conditions, is two shots behind early leader Joost Luiten. Spain's Eugenio Chacarra, who leads McIlroy by 533.93 points in the Race to Dubai standings - with 2,000 available to this week's winner - opened with a level-par 72, while third-placed American Patrick Reed struggled during a 75. "I think it was a pretty fair score," said six-time major winner McIlroy. "I could probably stand here and argue that I could have been better, but I could probably stand here and argue that I could have been worse as well. "I hit the ball well for the most part. It's tricky, the wind makes it tricky. The course set-up is a little more difficult than in previous years. "The greens are not like Yas Links (in Abu Dhabi) last week. They're not absolutely perfect, so you've got to have your patience a little bit on them too. Overall, happy with the score." Race to Dubai leader Eugenio Chacarra (left) is hoping to deny Rory McIlroy a record-equalling eighth title [Getty Images] Nine players - Chacarra, McIlroy, Reed, Casey Jarvis, Aaron Rai, Jon Rahm, Ryan Fox, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier - can still clinch the Race to Dubai, but only Chacarra and McIlroy can guarantee the season-long accolade with victory at Jumeirah Golf Estates this week. Northern Ireland's McIlroy, who is aiming to match Scotland's Colin Montgomerie's record of eight season-long crowns, birdied two of his opening four holes before giving a shot back at the fifth. He birdied the seventh and 11th, and while he took six at the par-five 14th, he finished with a two-putt birdie four to end joint third. "You can't win it on the first day, but you can certainly lose it," added McIlroy. "I played nicely, so there was never any threat of me shooting a bad one. "But it was possible today to go out there and shoot a couple over and feel like you were sort of out of the tournament. "To get off to a solid start was very important." Chacarra, who has won three times already this season, finished his front nine with three straight birdies to turn in two-under 34 but dropped shots at 13 and 15 to lie five back of Luiten. item.title: Dan Hicks, Longtime NBC Sports Broadcaster, Dies at 64
item.description: Credit: Getty Images Dan Hicks, the longtime NBC Sports broadcaster who spent 26 years as the network’s lead golf announcer and called some of the most memorable moments in Olympic swimming, died Wednesday following an acute illness. He was 64. Hicks joined NBC Sports in 1992 and became its lead golf play-by-play announcer in 2000, covering major tournaments including the U.S. Open and Ryder Cup. He also called Olympic swimming alongside analyst Rowdy Gaines, including Michael Phelps’ historic eight-gold-medal performance at the 2008 Beijing Games, as well as Notre Dame football and Olympic skiing. “Our family is heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected passing of Dan following an acute illness,” his wife, ESPN broadcaster Hannah Storm, said in a family statement published Thursday by Golf Channel. “He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many. His loss is immeasurable.” Among Hicks’ most memorable broadcasts were Tiger Woods’ dramatic putt to force a playoff at the 2008 U.S. Open and the American men’s swimming team’s comeback victory in the 4×100-meter freestyle relay at the Beijing Olympics that same year. He worked alongside longtime NBC golf analyst Johnny Miller for nearly two decades and became one of the network’s most familiar voices across major sporting events. A native of Tucson, Arizona, Hicks graduated from the University of Arizona and began his broadcasting career in local radio and television. He joined CNN in 1989, anchoring weekend editions of “CNN Sports Tonight” and hosting college football and basketball programming before moving to NBC three years later. His assignments at NBC also included NFL games, NBA coverage and Olympic speed skating. “Dan Hicks was an extraordinary colleague, friend and person,” NBC Sports executives Rick Cordella, Sam Flood and Molly Solomon said in a joint statement provided to TheWrap. “He was an exceptional storyteller and caller of games and events who elevated some of the biggest moments in sports history.” Versant CEO Mark Lazarus, who worked alongside Hicks for decades, said he was “heartbroken by the sudden loss of our friend,” remembering him as a loyal friend and devoted husband and father. Storm also remembered Hicks as someone who brought people together through his humor and kindness. “Our three daughters and I are heartbroken,” she said. “We are grateful for the love and support surrounding our family during this incredibly difficult time.” Hicks is survived by Storm and their daughters Hannah, Ellery and Riley. The post Dan Hicks, Longtime NBC Sports Broadcaster, Dies at 64 appeared first on TheWrap .

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned. What happens next?
item.description: After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation. However, The New York Times reported on Wednesday that there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him. A board meeting that night ended with Huang’s resignation , and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was installed as the new interim CEO. Recent reporting noted that since last year, US intelligence reports had identified Alice Huang (no relation) as not only the exec for an AI compute company renting access to Nvidia GPUs, but also a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. The second report focused on Huang and Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, claiming that a bystander who recorded the two being “affectionate” at the hotel hosting Nvidia’s GTC developer conference in May was met by Huang’s security workers and asked to sign a non-disclosure agreement. In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies, including the “neoclouds” like Coreweave who have been some of its biggest customers. Even Jensen Huang’s jackets aren’t safe from adulteration. AOC chimes in on the Nvidia CEO scandal. If Jensen Huang is done at Nvidia, who will be the next CEO? Johny Srouji? Nvidia is reportedly preparing to fire Jensen Huang When I asked who else Jensen Huang was fucking, I did not expect to get answers so quickly. Jensen Huang’s affair reportedly has Taiwan and US cabinet officials rattled. Nvidia hires the same law firm that investigated the Clippers to look into Jensen Huang’s spy. The US is winning the AI race. Jensen Huang could have blown it What could China get from Jensen Huang? Here’s what Trump said he knew about Jensen Huang The future of AI hinges on… Jensen Huang’s sex life? item.title: 5 Questions About Jessie Bates III: Jaguars ‘Hit the Jackpot’
item.description: Dec 29, 2025; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III (3) does an interview after a victory over the Los Angeles Rams at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Jacksonville Jaguars have traded for Jessie Bates III! To learn more about Duval’s newest starting safety, we went straight to the source. Here are 5 Questions with Jeanna Kelley, who covered Bates’ time with the Atlanta Falcons over the past three and a half seasons for SB Nation’s The Falcoholic . Question 1: Did the Falcons’ decision to trade Bates surprise you? Why did they feel comfortable making the move? I was not surprised by the Falcons’ decision to trade Jessie Bates. He is still playing at a high level right now, but he’ll be 30 in February, and he’s in a contract year. From a business standpoint, trading Bates—while he still offers so much to a competitive team like the Jags who look ready to win NOW—and getting quality draft capital in return makes a lot more sense than holding on to him in a lost season (sure, the Falcons COULD still win the disaster that is the NFC South, but if you’ve watched any of their losses you’ll understand why I think this is a long shot) and getting absolutely nothing for him. Don’t get me wrong — I’m not happy about the trade. Bates has a defensive touchdown in four consecutive seasons, and the intensity of his preparation and play have set the standard for Jeff Ulbrich’s defense. He will be a wonderful addition for the Jags. Question 2: Jaguars GM James Gladstone has made it clear he’s searching for “intangibly rich” players. What can you tell us about Jessie Bates as a person? If James Gladstone is looking for “intangibly rich” players, he hit the jackpot with Jessie Bates. Bates may be a better leader than player, and he’s an outstanding player. Many young players in Atlanta are better pros because of Bates’ influence. He leads by example, and you won’t find many players in this league with a stronger work ethic or leadership abilities than Bates. Get ready for game day with SB Nation’s new app! item.title: UFC’s Dana White Paid $1.5 Million for 2 Custom Ram Trucks at His First Car Auction: ‘I Like to Win’
item.description: THE BARRETT-JACKSON AUCTION COMPANY; ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA Dana White , UFC President and CEO, attended his very first car auction recently and ended up dropping $1.5 million on two custom Ram trucks. “I need another car like I need to lose more hair,” White joked in a pre-auction interview , but admitted he would bid anyway. “And I like to win.” The Barrett-Jackson 2026 Las Vegas Auction took place on September 11, and in remembrance of the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks, proceeds were shared between the Folds of Honor Foundation, which provides educational scholarships to the families of America’s fallen or disabled military and first responders, and the UFC Foundation, which will use the money to help support Hispanic charities. THE BARRETT-JACKSON AUCTION COMPANY “I’m grateful to UFC, Ram, RealTruck and Barrett-Jackson for this unique and very special opportunity,” said Folds of Honor founder and CEO Lt. Col. Dan Rooney in a press release . “The four companies are true patriots that are changing our recipients’ lives through education.” Because Barrett-Jackson, known as the world’s greatest collector car auction house, waived all fees and commissions, 100 percent of the hammer price went to the two charities. “Dana is one of the most patriotic individuals in our country, and it is fitting that his winning bid on 9/11 will benefit those in need, especially the families of fallen American service members and first responders,” Craig Jackson , chairman and CEO of the company, said in a press release . “It’s a great charity, it’s going to help a lot of people and I like that I’m leaving here with these two trucks,” White added after the auction. He got the first retail production and custom one-of-one 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee SRT Pickup and a pristine custom 2005 Ram 1500 SRT-10 Pickup, which were designed in collaboration between Ram, UFC, RealTruck and Barrett-Jackson. THE BARRETT-JACKSON AUCTION COMPANY “Every build tells a story. This one tells three. It’s a 2005 truck, the same year UFC’s Ultimate Fighter launched under Dana White and this SRT-10 became the inspiration for the new Rumble Bee it’s paired with,” RealTruck Inc. Vice President of Marketing Lee Riser said in a press release . “We took RealTruck’s product lineup, Ram’s performance DNA, and UFC’s massive platform, and pointed it all at something bigger: raising real money for Folds of Honor and the UFC Foundation through Barrett-Jackson’s stage,” he added. “This is how you build a legacy piece with a purpose and we’re excited to have this heavyweight added to our collaboration lineup.” Read More From National Enquirer Attorney Hit With $400,000 Fine for Exposing Priest’s Inappropriate Relationship Says It Was Worth It New York Man Pleads Guilty to $127 Million in Decade-Long Adult Daycare Fraud Scheme Man Accused of Attacking a Woman at the Yes Motel After She Refused to Do What He Asked This story UFC’s Dana White Paid $1.5 Million for 2 Custom Ram Trucks at His First Ca

item.title: McNabney set for debut as Irish make seven changes
item.description: McNabney could make his Test debut after recovering from a serious knee injury [Getty Images] Ulster's James McNabney is poised to make his Ireland debut off the bench as head coach Andy Farrell makes seven changes for Saturday's Nations Championship match against Fiji. In addition to a raft of personnel changes, Farrell has made two key positional switches with Nick Timoney and Mack Hansen moving to number eight and full-back. Timoney's switch comes amid an injury crisis at number eight, with Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Sean Jansen all ruled out through injury, while Hansen replaces Hugo Keenan, who drops out of the squad after scoring a hat-trick of tries in the 42-12 win over Argentina. Jamie Osborne, Bundee Aki, Tommy O'Brien and Jamison Gibson-Park are also drafted into the backline, with Rob Baloucoune and Sam Prendergast retained. In the pack, Ronan Kelleher starts at hooker with Dan Sheehan ruled out because of concussion, while James Ryan partners stand-in captain Tadhg Beirne in the second row as Joe McCarthy drops out. With Timoney switching to number eight, former World Rugby player of the year Josh van der Flier is recalled at open-side flanker. Horses, farming and a bad injury - McNabney's rise to Ireland recognition 'It's what I want' - Carbery outlines Ireland dream Ulster's Timoney 'grateful' for Ireland chances Were McNabney to be called upon, it would cap a remarkable ascent for the 23-year-old, who has started just one game for Ulster this season after recovering from the anterior cruciate ligament injury that forced him to miss the entire 2025-26 campaign. McNabney is one of four Ulster players on the bench alongside hooker Tom Stewart, prop Tom O'Toole and centre McCloskey, who drops out of the starting line-up for the first time in 2026. With back-to-back world champions South Africa bringing their much-vaunted scrum power to Dublin next week, Farrell has opted to stick with first-choice props Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong. Behind an experienced second row of Ryan and Beirne, Ryan Baird keeps his place at blind-side flanker after impressing on his return against Argentina, while Timoney is entrusted with a first Test start at number eight after an eye-catching showing at open-side last week. Back-up lock Darragh Murray is in line to win his fourth cap off the bench. With Keenan not included, Hansen returns to the full-back jersey. The 28-year-old scored a hat-trick of tries on his first start at 15 against Australia last year. Tommy O'Brien returns to left wing while Aki - a late withdrawal from the Argentina game because of illness - and Osborne represent a new centre partnership. Gibson-Park returns at scrum-half after Craig Casey was preferred last week, while Prendergast is retained at fly-half with Ciaran Frawley kept in reserve. Ireland sit third behind France and England in the Nations Championship northern hemisphere standings with three wins from four games. Fiji, who have never beaten Ireland, lost 52-17 to Fra

item.title: NBA Expert Makes Bold Celtics Declaration In Latest Power Rankings
item.description: NBA Expert Makes Bold Celtics Declaration In Latest Power Rankings originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . One NBA expert believes the Boston Celtics have already established themselves as the team to beat in the Eastern Conference. In his latest NBA power rankings, The Sporting News' Stephen Noh moved the Celtics up to No. 2, trailing only the San Antonio Spurs. "Paul George has been the perfect fit as a high-volume shooter that can still play good defense," wrote Noh . "They have room to get even better as Mitchell Robinson plays himself back into shape. "An impressive 22-point win over the Sixers reinforced that they're the best team in the East." MORE: Charles Barkley Calls Out Jaylen Brown Over Jayson Tatum Snub It's hard to argue with Noh's assessment based on how the Celtics have started the season. At 10-2, Boston owns the best record in the Eastern Conference. The Celtics have outscored their opponents by an average of 11.7 points per 100 possessions, giving them the NBA's best net rating . They also rank sixth in offensive efficiency and second in defensive efficiency. Noh predicted the Celtics would finish as the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference, but not everyone shared that optimism. The defending champion New York Knicks were a popular pick to return to the NBA Finals. The Philadelphia 76ers, Indiana Pacers and Toronto Raptors also received plenty of support as potential contenders . If Noh is right, the rest of the Eastern Conference has a serious problem on its hands. item.title: Arizona Fall League: Charles Davalan quiet in blowout win
item.description: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 13: Charles Davalan #6 of the Los Angeles Dodgers looks on from his defensive position at second base during a game between the Salt River Rafters and the Glendale Desert Dogs at Camelback Ranch on October 13, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) | Getty Images Beating the Scorpions 11-0 helped the Desert Dogs avoid ending the AFL regular season without reaching double-digit wins, securing their 10th victory in 27 games. Despite the massive result, the presence and impact of Dodger players in this game were somewhat limited, with only two taking part in it. Carrying on this second base experiment, Charles Davalan got the start and was the only hitter in Glendale’s lineup not to reach base safely, finishing the game 0 for 4, lowering his batting average to .221. Down in the ninth spot, Anson Aroz was responsible for scoring two of the Dessert Dogs’ 11 runs. Outside of an Aroz double, the only other Glendale batter to record extra-base hits in this game was Owen Carey (homer and a double), driving in five of the game’s 11 runs. Six Glendale pitchers combined to strike out 10 in seven scoreless frames. Wednesday score Glendale 11, Scottsdale 0 Thursday schedule It’s playoff time in the AFL with Glendale and Scottsdale meeting in a winner-take-all quarterfinal matchup starting at 12:30 a.m. (PT).

item.title: SEC school trying to flip 4-star recruit committed to Michigan Football
item.description: Zach Libby/Maize n Brew Welcome to the Recruiting Roundup, our twice-per-week series breaking down the latest developments on the recruiting trail for the Michigan Wolverines. We’ll keep you up to date on the top targets, the visits they take, the predictions that analysts make, and everything in between. Here’s what you need to know today… Ole Miss making a push for Michigan commit Michigan has a recruitment to watch closely in its secondary, as flip predictions have been entered favoring 2027 four-star defensive back Tavares Harrington to flip to Ole Miss. The Chicago Mount Carmel prospect committed to Michigan on May 22, choosing the Wolverines over a group of finalists that included the Rebels. Ole Miss has continued to pursue the 6-foot-3 defender and now appears to be a serious threat to pull him away. Harrington remains committed to Michigan, but losing him would be another setback in the secondary after four-star safety Darrell Mattison flipped from the Wolverines to Ole Miss back in May. The development comes as Kyle Whittingham’s staff works to reassure commitments following offensive coordinator Jason Beck’s dismissal. Whittingham said he and the staff reached out to every recruit and received positive responses. “We got on the phone with every recruit (Sunday) night,” Whittingham said. “And they seemed to be very receptive and positive. Nobody was panicking.” The Wolverines have work to do with Harrington. The predictions don’t make the flip official just yet, but they give fans reason to keep a close eye on this one. Four-star edge commit remains solid despite Tennessee visit Another Michigan commitment visited an SEC school over the weekend, but the circumstances should ease concerns about his future. According to Ethan McDowell of The Wolverine , 2027 four-star edge commit Ifeanyi Emedobi planned to return to Ann Arbor before a family obligation prevented the trip. Instead, the Fort Wayne Northrop prospect joined a group from Traction Athletic Performance, where he trains, for Tennessee’s game against Kentucky. The Volunteers have not offered Emedobi and were not actively recruiting him at the time of McDowell’s report. Tennessee took his measurements and indicated the staff might reach back out to him, but he had not heard from the program afterward. Even while in Knoxville, Emedobi was keeping tabs on Michigan’s game against Michigan State. A source close to his recruitment put it simply to McDowell: “Ife loves Michigan.” His relationships with defensive line coaches Lewis Powell, Larry Black and David Denham remain a major reason he feels comfortable with his pledge. “Communication’s been great,” Emedobi said earlier this fall. “We talk every day of the week.” Emedobi still plans to enroll at Michigan in January. McDowell’s assessment is that a coaching change along the defensive line would be the development that could give the Wolverines something to worry about. item.title: Our Defense vs. Their Offense: Carolina Panthers
item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 08: Carl Granderson #96 of the New Orleans Saints lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Cleveland Browns at Cesars Superdome on November 8, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images In what is an unconventional matchup for the top spot in the division, the 3-5 Saints will host the 3-5 Panthers on Sunday at noon in the Superdome. The Panthers came out hot to start the season, and it looked like head coach Dave Canales had finally figured out how to get the team to progress around QB Bryce Young. The Panthers were, at one point, 3-2 and sitting in the top spot of the NFC South, and Bryce Young was playing the best football of his NFL career. Since then, the Panthers have lost three straight games, including a blowout loss to the Bucs. The Panthers have still made strides offensively, even though they have been on this losing streak. Currently, the Panthers have the fourth-best passing offense in the NFL, averaging over 261 yards per game. Through the first eight games of the season, Young has thrown for 2,197 yards, 16 TDs, and six INTs. Right now, Young is on pace to finish the season with over 4,500 yards and 34 TDs. Overall, the Panthers are ninth in the NFL in total offense, averaging 362 yards per game, and 11th in scoring, averaging 24.9 points per game. None of these categories are favorable to the Saints’ defense, as they are currently allowing 370.5 total yards per game, 27 points per game, 236 passing yards per game, and 133.9 rushing yards per game, ranking 27th or worse in the NFL in each category. The Panthers have the advantage in both rushing and passing, and they have a true No. 1 receiving threat in Tetairoa McMillan. McMillan has recorded 46 receptions for 625 yards and three TDs so far this season. This could present a matchup problem for the Saints’ cornerbacks. The Saints are currently tied for eighth-most in completions of 20-plus yards allowed, having surrendered 28 through eight games. The big-play opportunities are there for opponents, especially considering that not only are those plays available, but there haven’t been many consequences for attempting them, as the Saints have only four INTs on the season. There are two key areas the Saints can attack. The Carolina offense has been awful at the line of scrimmage when it comes to protecting the QB. The Panthers’ offense has allowed 26 sacks so far this year, averaging 3.25 sacks allowed per game. They have also allowed 104 pressures this year, which is roughly 13 pressures per game. The Saints have the best pass-rushing duo in the NFL in Chase Young and Carl Granderson. The issue with the Saints’ pass rush is that their pressure rate is still a little low, considering how dominant that pair of edge rushers has been. The Saints currently rank just 26th in the league in pressure rate, which means that if it’s not Young or Granderson, the pressure isn’t consistently getting through.

item.title: The 28-year old Europa League winner turned director and photographer
item.description: The 28-year old Europa League winner turned director and photographer Former Tottenham goalkeeper Alfie Whiteman says football is a “different world” from what he is doing now. Whiteman was part of the Tottenham squad that won the Europa League in 2026. At only 27 years old, the former footballer has since left his boyhood club, not to pursue football elsewhere, but instead to enter the art world. His project, ‘Alfie Whiteman, A Loan’, was launched at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in May 2026. There, he showcased photos from his loan spells at Degerfors in Sweden and highlighted his transition from footballer to director and photographer. Although his work has accelerated since the end of his football career, Whiteman revealed that his art projects began long before he hung up his boots. “It sort of started many years prior,” he told Hayters.com at the launch of Together Tottenham. “When I was kind of 17, 18 and full-time, I realised that I was interested in other things and was using my spare time to get on set and get experience and, you know, plan for life after football because I knew how short a career it was. “Ultimately, I was sort of living a double life, using my days off to try and do what I could outside, so when that day did come, I’d have some experience. “And then I got to a point where I decided that I actually just wanted to kind of explore these other things myself and not wait for retirement age.” Whiteman was part of a Spurs squad alongside players such as Harry Kane, Heung-min Son and Dele Alli. “I kind of didn’t really shout about things,” he said when asked what the rest of the squad thought. “But all the players are wonderful. I had so many, you know, good friendships. “But I would say I didn’t kind of fully talk about everything because it was somewhat of a different world to the other things I was doing.” Although he says football and his art career are different worlds, Whiteman explained how many of the skills he learned while playing still benefit him in his new ventures. “I was a sort of lifelong fan and a mascot as a kid, but I feel football, you know, taught me a lot of things that I’m realising are very transferable into what I’m doing now. “I think I was very lucky and fortunate to kind of have those wonderful experiences. All the hard work and sacrifice that it took. “I feel like even when I’m doing these other things, I’m seeing the value in it.”

item.title: Thursday Rockpile: Are any of the MLB-bound NPB pitchers fits for the Rockies?
item.description: TOKYO, JAPAN - MARCH 07: Hiromi Itoh #14 of Team Japan pitches in the fourth inning during the 2026 World Baseball Classic Pool C game between South Korea and Japan at Tokyo Dome on March 07, 2026 in Tokyo, Japan. (Photo by Gene Wang - Capture At Media/Getty Images) | Getty Images As has become an annual tradition, a collection of high profile players from Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB), the league with the second highest talent level in the world, may be headed to MLB this offseason. In October, Purple Row’s Skyler Timmins looked at whether Teruaki Sato, the highest profile position player expected to make the jump from Japan this offseason, was a fit for the Rockies . The biggest offseason need for the Rockies, however, is on the mound. None of the NPB pitchers available this offseason are expected to translate into the sort of top-of-the-rotation ace that someone like Yoshinobu Yamamoto has become since his MLB debut in 2024, but that does not mean there are zero talented arms. The question is, are any of them fits for what the Rockies need? Hiromi Itoh (伊藤 大海) Age: 29 2026 NPB stats: 3.23 ERA, 2.81 FIP, & 159 strikeouts over 172.2 innings pitched Contract context: Posted by the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters After taking home the 2025 Sawamura award (the NPB equivalent to a Cy Young award), Hiromi Itoh took a step backwards this past season. He remained as durable as ever, reaching the 150-inning mark for the fifth straight season, but saw his ERA spike from a very good 2.52 in 2025 up to a roughly league-average 3.23 while playing his home games at ES CON field, NPB’s most hitter friendly ballpark . This drop in run prevention corresponded with a drop in fastball velocity. Yuri Karasawa characterized the drop this way on a recent episode of Baseball Bar-B-Cast : “Itoh is a very different pitcher when he’s sitting 91/92 which is where he was this year, and then like 93/94 which is where he was in the second half of 2025.” Fangraphs Eric Longenhagen, in an extensive piece covering many notable pro’s in NPB and KBO , had the following to say about Itoh: Itoh’s stuff is pretty light. He’s durable (at least 146 innings pitched in every year since 2021) and throws strikes (fewer than two walks per nine innings in each of the last three years), but he sits 92 mph and generates roughly average-or-below miss and chase on all of his pitches. He’s a high-floored backend starter, but he’s not the type of guy who moves the needle on a postseason staff. Overall, his impeccable track record and enormous arsenal of pitch types (depending on how you slice it he has as many as 13 different pitch grips) mean that Itoh is as close to a safe bet as it comes to be able to make the transition from NPB to MLB and remain a starting pitcher. What’s more, it’s possible (though not likely), that if he were able to regain his 2025 velocity that he could outperform that back-of-rotation projection. item.title: Georgia Tech Football: Things I Think I Know – Clemson
item.description: For the first time since I have been writing for FTRS, I don’t just think I know; I know. I know that we are a bad, bad football team. There is little, if anything, positive to say about our lackluster performance against Louisville, and it doesn’t get easier from here as we head to Death Valley to take on the Clemson Tigers. Here is what I think I know as we inch closer to the end of this dreadful 2026 season. This isn’t Dabo’s typical Clemson anymore. Clemson is not the beast that they used to be, but they are still good enough to do some serious damage against us. Thankfully for us, they are not as offensively competent as they were in Dabo Swinney’s earlier years as head coach. This has arguably been his first year coaching in which he has had major quarterback troubles. The Tigers started the year with senior Christopher Vizzina at quarterback, but after his troubling performance against LSU, they quickly turned to true freshman Tait Reynolds. He has been their starter ever since, with 1,446 yards on the year and a QBR of 41.0. Because they are an ACC foe, I have witnessed a lot of Clemson football in my life, and this is the worst they have been on offense by a landslide. They are 115th in the country in total offense, averaging 338 yards per game. I will commend them, though; the Tigers have been in a lot of close games this year, yet have figured out how to come out on top. A big factor in that has been their defense. They are only allowing 334.9 yards per game, and this has been enough to get the job done despite their uninspired offense. They reached bowl eligibility last week and have only lost to LSU, Miami, and Virginia Tech this season. So, while they are not Dabo’s superpower Clemson anymore, they have done enough to most likely have a winning season and keep Dabo’s streak of being bowl-eligible alive. Because both teams are having offensive struggles, I could see this game ending in a 24-7 score, as it is quite literally the definition of a 12:30 slot on the CW. Key has lost the locker room, but he has begun to make necessary changes. It feels like the team’s morale is at an all-time low, and frankly, I cannot blame the players for feeling that way. These players do not understand their assignments on the field, and Key even said after the Boston College game that they looked “panicked.” This was especially evident when a defender ran into a linebacker while Louisville’s Tre Richardson scampered down the field for a 52-yard touchdown. As a fan, I feel little to no emotion when watching my alma mater play football. It’s a sad situation to be in, but Tech fans finally got the news we have been waiting for. As of Monday afternoon, defensive coordinator Jason Semore, defensive ends coach Kyle Pope, offensive line coach Allen Mogridge, and wide receivers coach Jafar Williams have been dismissed. item.title: Manu Ginobili's signed, game-worn Nikes score big at auction
item.description: Top bid throwback: a signed, game-used pair of Manu Ginobili Nike Air Uptempo player-exclusive sneakers worn by the Spurs star 20 years ago. (Courtesy Goldin) When is a Manu Ginobili autograph worth more than $9,000? When it's Sharpie'd on a pair of shoes the Spurs great wore 20 years ago. A twice-signed pair of Ginobili game-used Nike Air Uptempo Pro player exclusive sneakers recently sold at auction at Goldin for $9,394. The winning bid clocked in at $7,700, but the price spikes with the buyer's premium fee at 22% of the final bid price. The player-exclusive Manu Ginobili Nike Air Uptempos feature the Spurs star's autograph and jersey number. Ginobili wore the sneakers for two games in 2006. (Courtesy Goldin) Manu Ginobili signed the toebox of both sneakers. (Courtesy Goldin) The black kicks with the silver swoosh feature Ginobili's signature monogram "MG" logo on the tongue and his jersey No. 20 on the heels. Ginobili signed each sneaker inside the toebox with silver ink. Of course, that was after he laced them up for a couple of West Coast wins in 2006. Gotta be the Manu shoes. (Jeff Gross/Getty Images) The sneakers were photo-matched to two games Ginobili played with the Spurs in Los Angeles at what was then called the Staples Center: a 98-87 win against the Clippers on March 28 and a 96-85 win against the Lakers two nights later. ZOUNDS: Texan pulls Spurs star Dylan Harper's rookie card valued at nearly $3 million Spurs great Manu Ginobili handles the ball against the Los Angeles Clippers on March 28, 2006, at Staples Center in Los Angeles, Calif. Two decades later, the shoes he wore for the game would sell for $9,000. (Jeff Gross/Getty Images) Spurs star Manu Ginobili puts up a shot as the Los Angeles Lakers' Kobe Bryant, left, Lamar Odom (7), and Brian Cook, right, guard during the first half of the NBA basketball game March 30, 2006, in Los Angeles. Ginobili wore the same shoes as he did two nights prior against the Clippers. (MARK J. TERRILL/AP) In the Clippers game, Ginobili scored eight points with a game-high nine assists and three steals. Against the Lakers, he racked up 11 points, four assists, a couple of rebounds and a game-high three steals. The shoes have the wear to show it. According to the auction description, the Nikes sported game use and aging, including creasing, emblem yellowing, loose stitching and scuff marks. The sold sneakers came with a MeiGray letter of authenticity confirming game use and Beckett letters of authenticity for the signatures. No word if they also came with a pair of Sneaker Balls. item.title: Scouting Report: SMU Mustangs
item.description: DALLAS, TX - NOVEMBER 06: SMU Mustangs quarterback Kevin Jennings (7) throws a pass during the Atlantic Coast Conference college football game between the SMU Mustangs and the Virginia Tech Hokies on November 6, 2026, at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Basics Team : SMU Mustangs Location : Dallas, Texas Enrollment : 12,544 Head Coach : Rhett Lashlee (43-18) Record : 7-2 (5-2) Wins : FSU, UC Davis, Missouri State, BC, UVA, Cal, VT Losses : Louisville, Syracuse Recruiting Rank : 38 (3 4-stars, 19 3-stars) Transfer Portal Rank : 32 (3 4-stars, 13 3-stars) Win Total : 8.5 Spread : Wake – 3.5 Wake Forest has maybe the biggest game in program history this week, taking on a 7-2 SMU team with major ACC Conference Championship implications on the line. With just 3 games remaining in the season, a win would keep the Deacs alone in 2nd place in the conference and give them a tie breaker over SMU. In that scenario, Wake probably only has to win 1 of their remaining 2 games to make it to Charlotte. A loss would drop Wake into a 5-way tie for 2nd place—the Deacs would have to finish the season 2-0 and hope for a favorable tie-break scenario. The new ACC tie-break policy for a 3+ team tie uses a “Team Success Ranking” metric which is not public, but one would have to assume beating ACC teams by 40+ points would improve that ranking significantly. Offense Points per game : 37.0 (19th out of 138 teams) Yards per game : 475.8 (11) Run/pass : 51% run, 49% pass Rush yards per game : 154.2 (70) Pass yards per game : 321.6 (7) 3rd down conversions : 48% (20) Sacks allowed per game : 1.6 (47) Turnovers : 12 (75) Based on the above stats, it’s pretty clear that the SMU offense will be the second best offense Wake has faced so far this season, behind only Miami. Despite the nearly balanced run-pass split, this is an offense that starts and goes with the passing game and QB Kevin Jennings. Jennings is one of the best quarterbacks in the nation and sits at 5th in the country in both passing yards and passing touchdowns. He will be the 5th QB Wake has played this season who is top 25 in the nation in passing yards (Jennings, Mensah, Kienholz, Browne, Warren). A quick glance at the offensive profile of the Mustangs from Game On Paper shows just how important the passing game is for this team. SMU is currently in the 90th percentile or above in passing success rate, yards per dropback, pass EPA/Play, and pass explosive percentage. For the season, Jennings is completing 74% of his passes for 2,764 yards 25 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. He is extremely mobile in the pocket and has a rocket arm that allows him to make throws with basically any arm angle and without having his feet set. item.title: Race for the College Football Playoff Week 11: Two Unbeatens Remain
item.description: GLENDALE, AZ - JANUARY 08: The ESPN CFP logo on a TV camera before the Miami Hurricanes versus Ole Miss Rebels College Football Playoff Semifinal at the VRBO Fiesta Bowl on January 8, 2026 at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Kevin Abele/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The latest CFP rankings are out with only two unbeaten teams remaining …. UCLA and Utah … just like we all predicted in the preseason. As for Mizzou — the Tigers are still ranked — coming in at No. 22. Missouri will need a miracle to make the playoff — starting with a road game at No. 1 Georgia on Saturday afternoon. Needless to say, Mizzou will have their hands full on Saturday. Big Ten favorite: UCLA The Bruins are 9-0 and ranked No. 4 in the latest CFP rankings coming off a 34-20 road win at Minnesota. Who had this coming? Is Bob Chesney the next Curt Cignetti? UCLA hosts Illinois on Friday night. ACC favorite: Miami (FL) Despite a 31-24 loss at Note Dame last week (without Malachi Toney), the Canes still look the part of National Championship contenders. Notre Dame hosts Boston College on Saturday as their remaining schedule is favorable down the stretch. Group of Six automatic bid: Boise State The Broncos are 8-1 and ranked No. 24 in the latest CFP rankings after a 64-38 road win over Colorado State last week. Boise State hosts Oregon State in the College Gameday game on Saturday, but quarterback Maddux Madsen is questionable. At-Large Bid Selections : Alabama : The Crimson Tide delivered a dominant 31-13 road win over LSU last week to prove their top-5 ranking. Alabama is at Vanderbilt on Saturday. Texas: Arch Manning and the Longhorns found a way with a 34-20 road win over Mizzou last week with some help from the officials ( somewhat kidding ). Texas’ resume is top-notch, and another opportunity awaits them at LSU on Saturday night. Tennessee : The Vols jump back into the playoff picture after a convincing win 34-6 win over Kentucky last week. Tennessee is at Texas A&M on Saturday in a game they can’t afford to lose. item.title: Max Verstappen Says He’d Never Sign Two No. 1 Drivers After Ferrari’s Mexico Clash
item.description: Max Verstappen says he would never sign two number-one drivers, pointing to Ferrari’s clash between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in Mexico. Ferrari is again dealing with two number-one drivers. It had the same problem when Sebastian Vettel was paired with Leclerc, and again when Carlos Sainz partnered the Monegasque. Now it’s Hamilton and Leclerc. The last few races have brought incidents at Monza and Mexico, and Mexico was the biggest talking point, leading to a chat between Hamilton and Leclerc . It’s rare for Ferrari F1 team principal Frederic Vasseur to show his disappointment in public, but he did, reminding both his drivers that “Ferrari is important.” Hamilton and Leclerc also had a run-in in Brazil , though that one was less heated. Verstappen Says Two Lead Drivers Is the Problem Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton in parc fermé after the sprint at the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix. Image Credit: Mark Thompson/Getty Images/Red Bull Content Pool When Viaplay asked Red Bull’s Verstappen about it, he said a team needs a clear number one and a clear number two to work properly. “If you simply had one clear number one and one clear number two, they would have gone through that corner in first and second, and they would have finished first and second as well,” said Verstappen, recalling how things panned out in Mexico for Ferrari. “Or maybe first and third, but that’s fine too. As a team, you’re still scoring good points. I’ve said it before. People very often disagree with me, but if I were a team principal – if I had my own team – I would never sign two number-one drivers, because then you get this. “Then this is normal. One isn’t going to give way to the other, because, of course, they both think they can win, and that’s how I am too. So, if I were a team principal, I would never go for two number-one drivers. Some people completely disagree with that, but that’s fine as well,” summed up Verstappen. Verstappen and Charles Leclerc after qualifying at the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix. Image Credit: Michael Potts/LAT Images/Getty Images/Red Bull Content Pool Verstappen Says a Team With a Good Car Just Needs a Decent No. 2 Verstappen admitted a team doesn’t always get to choose, but said two lead drivers make life harder inside it. “Sometimes you might not have a choice in that either, but [having two lead drivers] does make everything more complicated,” Verstappen said. He added that F1 history shows the setup works. “If you have a good car, then you don’t necessarily need that either, two number-one drivers. Just a decent number two,” Verstappen said. “Throughout Formula 1 history, it’s also always been clear that something like that works perfectly well, even for years.”

item.title: Panthers vs Saints: How injuries will dictate this week’s storylines
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Corey Thornton #31 of the Carolina Panthers reacts to his interception against the Denver Broncos during the second quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! We’re on to another game week, which means we can look forward to another game of football to hopefully wipe the slate clean and get Carolina moving in the right direction again. This week, the Panthers will travel to New Orleans to face my personal most hated division rival, the New Orleans Saints. What better way to bounce back from a loss against Sean Payton’s Broncos than defeating his former team? That math maths, right? The Panthers designated RB Jonathon Brooks, WR Xavier Legette, and CB Mike Jackson to return from injured/reserve this week, joining OL Brady Christensen whom they designated to return last week. So the Panthers appear to be finally getting reinforcements soon, which is why I decided to devote this week’s Storylines piece to the Panthers current injury situation on both sides of the ball. The team may not get any of those 4 guys back for this week, that will be dictated by how their practices go over the coming days and how the medical staff evaluates them. So let’s take a look at their current situations on offense and defense. Offense: The Offensive Line is getting healthier, but can they bounce back? On top of the aforementioned Brooks, Christensen, and Legette, OG Damien Lewis practiced in full on Wednesday. He has been the Panthers best offensive linemen when healthy this season, and his presence has been sorely missed. So depending on what happens with Brady Christensen, the Panthers could have two key offensive linemen returning this week. But honestly, the Panthers offensive line wasn’t as bad this past weekend as they have been previously, but they still allowed pressure and sacks leading to turnovers in very key situations. This week, they draw a Saints defense that isn’t the best as far as yardage per game is concerned, but they can pressure the passer. And in recent history, this defense has given Carolina’s offense fits. Of all games to right the trend of losses against New Orleans, this is the week, as Carolina still sits at number one in the NFC South despite their recent string of losses. They need to keep Bryce Young upright to take advantage of the Saints bottom third of the league defense in most statistical categories. Defense: The secondary again a storyline I’m not expecting Mike Jackson to return this week, but him being activated gives the Panthers about 3 weeks to evaluate him and decide if he’s healthy. But, there’s more good news in the secondary as Will Lee III managed a full practice on Wednesday. In addition, the Panthers finally activated Corey Thornton on Sunday, and he managed a really nice interception as the Panthers defense had a relatively okay game. item.title: Anything but Fighting: Stephen Thompson loves anime
item.description: NEW YORK, NY — UFC welterweight contender Stephen Thompson speaks with MMA Fighting’s José Youngs about his lifelong love of anime on Anything But Fighting. In terms of competing, Thompson (17-9-1) will be making the walk to the octagon for the final time of his career against Charles Radtke at UFC 334 in Madison Square Garden. Entering the contest, “Wonderboy” has struggled to add wins in recent years after dropping Shavkat Rakhmonov, Joaquin Buckley, and Gabriel Bonfim in his three most recent bouts. item.title: Our Defense vs Their Offense: Texas Longhorns
item.description: BATON ROUGE, LA - OCTOBER 17: DJ Pickett #5 of the LSU Tigers plays against the Mississippi State Bulldogs during the first half of a game at Tiger Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With the LSU offense still seeming to be the most inconsistent part of the team, the LSU defense will need to deliver a performance similar to the 2011 LSU defense in order to win this game. LSU’s defense has been very good all year, and the challenge is not going to get any easier. The responsibility for keeping the Tigers’ hopes of a major postseason appearance alive will fall squarely on their shoulders. The Tigers are set to take on the Longhorns this Saturday night in what will be the final home game of Lane Kiffin’s first year at LSU. Texas is led by Arch Manning, a New Orleans native and grandson of Saints legend Archie Manning. Arch Manning has had a solid campaign so far this season, and even though Texas has two losses, the Longhorns are still in control of their own destiny. Having Manning leading this offense certainly gives them a better chance of accomplishing their goals. So far this season, Manning has 2,024 passing yards with 18 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also completed 66% of his passes and averages around 225 passing yards per game. This Texas team has the ability to play similarly to the Alabama team that LSU just faced. When looking at the numbers, Alabama’s offense is statistically better in every single category, but the differences are not overwhelming. Texas averages 31.1 points per game, which ranks 48th nationally. The Longhorns also average 363 yards per game, ranking 87th nationally. Texas averages 232 passing yards and 130 rushing yards per game, ranking 66th and 105th nationally, respectively. This offense is not as good as the Alabama offense that just left Tiger Stadium with only 280 total yards. The major difference will be how defensive coordinator Blake Baker approaches Texas’ offensive philosophy. Texas uses a pro-style spread offense, whereas Alabama operates more out of a spread system with aggressive passing concepts. Texas uses motion to create leverage against opposing defenses and is comfortable taking what the defense gives them. The Longhorns also use motion to disguise what they are trying to accomplish on a given play. Credit head coach Steve Sarkisian, because against Missouri this past weekend, Texas began implementing more traditional spread principles, formations, and concepts to get the ball out of Manning’s hands quicker. This approach will probably be used frequently against LSU to combat the elite pass rush that the Tigers possess. Through nine games, Texas has allowed 27 sacks and has suffered significant injuries on the offensive side of the ball, most notably to left tackle Trevor Goosby. item.title: Syracuse Football: what to watch for vs NC State
item.description: SYRACUSE, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 31: Tylik Hill #20 of the Syracuse Orange moves the ball against Jamal Anderson #32 of the SMU Mustangs during the second quarter at JMA Wireless Dome on October 31, 2026 in Syracuse, New York. (Photo by Rebecca Villagracia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Two 4-5 teams trying to get one step closer to bowl eligibility will meet in Raleigh on Saturday. The Syracuse Orange (4-5, 2-5) visit the NC State Wolfpack (4-5, 2-4) and kickoff is at Noon on ACC Network. NC State is close to finalizing the deal to make Philip Rivers their next Head Coach , so will the Orange be able to spoil the party in Raleigh? Here’s what we’re watching for in this one: Kevin: Runnin’ in Raleigh NC State gave up 238 yards rushing to Duke last week and with Syracuse’s passing game having trouble against Clemson, look for a heavy dose of Ahmad Miller and Tylik Hill in this one. The Wolfpack are expected to be missing two of their top three tacklers so even with some injuries on the offensive line, I think the Orange need to try and control the pace and force NC State to commit to stopping the run. Hopefully this can open up some plays to Hatcher and Russell on the outside and force the defense to adjust. Dom: Offensive execution Bottom-line: the defense did its job against an albeit not great Clemson offense, but it put Syracuse in position to win and the offense just couldn’t capitalize. Even a slightly better performance from Steve Angeli makes the difference. He’s not the only one to blame (although the two turnovers were killer): Syracuse had just 3.5 yards per rush against Clemson, and as Kevin noted, the run game should be in line for a bounce back against the shaky Wolfpack defense. That alone should be enough, but the Orange can’t get in their own way again. ********************************************************************************************** What are you watching for in this one?

item.title: Bo Bichette’s down year led him right back to the Mets in 2027
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 29: Bo Bichette #19 of the New York Mets reacts after being called out against the Houston Astros during the game at Citi Field on August 29, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caean Couto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bo Bichette, a former second round draft pick of the Blue Jays and son of four-time All-Star Dante Bichette, authored one of the biggest plays of the iconic Game 7 of the 2025 World Series when he cracked a three-run home run off Shohei Ohtani in the third inning. At the time, it was impossible to imagine Bichette, a two-time All-Star with Toronto, as anything other than a Blue Jay for life, despite his impending free agency. It seemed like he and the Jays were inextricably linked, and his return that winter was a mere formality. Then, a series of unforeseen events happened along the way, as they often do in the MLB offseason. The Mets let their own homegrown star Pete Alonso, sign elsewhere, and they traded another, Brandon Nimmo, to the Rangers. In an effort to beef up their offense, they made an aggressive play for Kyle Tucker, who ended up with the Dodgers on a short-term, high-AAV deal. Needing something to appease the fanbase and looking to plug a hole in their lineup, they landed Bichette within 24 hours of losing out on Tucker, much to the surprise of the entire league. The deal was for $126 million over three years ($42 million AAV), with opts out strategically offered after each year. The deal seemed, at the time, like a win for both sides. Given his age, the high AAV, and the ability to re-enter the market in search of that elusive long-term contract, it seemed like the marriage would be convenient for both parties. Thomas Henderson, in his Bichette season preview , went so far as to predict the following: The Mets and Bichette agreed to the three-year deal, but in all actuality it is likely a one-year contract…In all likelihood, Bichette will perform well enough to forgo the $84 million left on his contract to chase long-term stability, which is part of the reason why the Mets were into him in the first place. To Thomas’ credit, this was an extremely rational and level-headed prediction, and one that I’d guess 99% of Mets fans envisioned when the deal was announced. However, a not-so-funny thing happened along the way: Bichette performed well below his career norms, becoming one of the most disappointing Mets during the course of an overly-frustrating 2026 season. As a result, the near-certainty of his opt out has reversed, and Bichette exercised his player option for 2027. Given his overall numbers and the uncertainty associated with the looming lockout, it’s hard to blame him. Bichette fell victim to one of the most common occurrences of star players coming to New York—the slow start. And oh boy, was it ever slow. Bichette gave fans immediate buyer’s remorse with a 2-for-22 start over his first five games. He strung together hits in 10 of his next 11 games and raised his slash line to .250/.30

item.title: Elephant Rumblings: Is Jacob Wilson A Trade Candidate?
item.description: SACRAMENTO, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 16: Jacob Wilson #5 of the Athletics bunts into a force out during the third inning against the Texas Rangers at Sutter Health Park on August 16, 2026 in Sacramento, California. (Photo by Scott Marshall/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Thursday A’s fans! There has been a report making the rounds online that young shortstop Jacob Wilson could be on the trade block this offseason thanks to USA Today’s Bob Nightengale: Athletics infielder Jacob Wilson is a potential trade chip as the club searches for starting pitching, per @BNightengale While the A’s have “zero urgency to trade him,” Nightengale notes they’re desperate for starting pitching and Wilson could be a valuable trade chip Wilson is… pic.twitter.com/NNwr2iF2q5 — Nosebleed Baseball (@Baseball_NBS) November 9, 2026 That’s begun a larger-than-expected debate about Wilson’s trade value and whether or not the Athletics would really consider trading him. On it’s face it seems like a far-fetched idea for the A’s to even consider moving Wilson, let alone pulling the trigger on a trade to eject their starting shortstop. The A’s are one year away from making the move to Las Vegas. Don’t we want some core players around when the new stadium opens? Wilson will be turning 25 at the beginning of next season. That’s around the time a lot of players even make it to the big leagues, let alone establish themselves. Establishing himself is an understatement for Wilson after he started the All-Star Game in 2025 as a rookie. That earned him a nice contract extension, getting $70 million early to tie him to the A’s for the next seven years. Granted, his sophomore campaign wasn’t as thrilling as his rookie season but a lot of that can probably be chalked up to fluke injuries. Wilson was having a fine campaign before the All-Star break, and dumping him now would be at a sell-low point for a young player locked into a long-term deal. On the other hand, there are obvious reasons to consider a swap if it makes sense. Wilson did after all have a tough second half, and then to cap his year off he underwent major shoulder surgery. While the expectation is that he’ll be fully healed and good to go come Spring Training, shoulders have been known to be tricky sometimes. If the club believes that his shoulder could become a recurring problem that they don’t want to deal with regularly, they could be more amenable to moving him we think. While it sounds far fetched, it really does make sense to at least consider it on paper. The contract isn’t especially onerous, even for small-market teams. He’s affordable for even the lowest-payroll teams and that broadens the potential market if the A’s really wanted to make Wilson available. New President Taylor Smith isn’t connected to Wilson at all and might not be as enamored with him as other teams may be. Wilson’s contact-oriented approach would make lots of slugging teams more balanced. And then you have the roster fit. The A’s best prospect

item.title: Patrick Mahomes doesn’t expect a long learning period for Josh Downs
item.description: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Tuesday, the Kansas City Chiefs executed a trade with the Indianapolis Colts to bring in wide receiver Josh Downs in return for a pair of Day 3 draft selections. Now that the move is official, the process of integrating Downs into the offense begins. Speaking before Wednesday’s practice, quarterback Patrick Mahomes did not foresee a problem. Mahomes expects his new target to be on the field as he learns Kansas City’s offense. “It is realistic,” Mahomes explained, “because we do a great job of kind of moving guys in and out of every single position, and so guys know the entire concepts of the plays. We’re very detailed with how we call the plays in the huddle, which will help him out a ton. Then when he doesn’t know, being able to talk to me in the huddle or talk to the guys as they’re breaking the huddle, and that usually helps when the guys like each other. “It’s good to have a guy that you can tell everybody’s going to like and that he has his head on the right way and he’s going to make sure that he’s going to do whatever it takes to win.” Mahomes has no question about what Downs brings to the Chiefs. Daniel Jones dropped it in the bucket for Josh Downs @INDvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pqCXVQd3Yg — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 “He does a great job of winning one-on-one matchups,” observed Mahomes, “which is always important. He runs routes really well. He sets them up really well, where he will run a route early in the game that he sets up for another one later in the game. “Then he has really good feel,” Mahomes said. “Obviously, playing in the system that he has — he has a lot of read-type routes, and you can tell he knows how to get himself open, settle in the right zones, and win versus man when he can. So, I think it will be an easy transition for him to kind of do that stuff in our offense. Then with how we do things, he can play a lot of different positions as we move receivers and tight ends around.” Speaking after Mahomes, Downs explained the obvious answer to how he will work himself into the system. “When [Mahomes] throws me the ball, just catch it,” he remarked, “and keep making plays when he throws it to me and do anything I can to learn the offense as fast as possible. “I don’t want to be a guy that’s asking everybody what the play is or what the formation is,” Downs pointed out. “I feel like that’s when you kind of get left behind. So, I want to do everything I can to learn as fast as possible.” Mahomes elaborated on the learning ahead of Downs, who he believes is up for the challenge after seeing his attention in Wednesday’s walk through. “The entire offense will probably take a couple weeks,” he predicted, “but I think what I’ve learned just from meeting Josh is he’s very intelligent. item.title: Gossip: Roma drop interest in Barcelona outcast Alejandro Balde
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - OCTOBER 31: Alejandro Balde of FC Barcelona looks on during the Spanish league, LaLiga EA Sports, football match played between FC Barcelona and Deportivo Alaves at Spotify Camp Nou stadium on October 31, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo By Javier Borrego/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images Serie A side Roma have reportedly dropped interest in Barcelona defender Alejandro Balde ahead of the January transfer window. Roma had been linked with the left-back, along with a host of other clubs including Juventus and Manchester United, but are now going cold on the defender, according to Il Messaggero. The Italian daily reports the club are now focusing on their attack instead and have put Balde interest on hold, potentially with a view to giving up altogether. Instead, Roma are thinking about trying to bring in Endrick from Real Madrid and Ademola Lookman from Atletico Madrid to boost their frontline. Balde’s future is likely to remain the subject of speculation as the left-back continues to struggle for game time at Barcelona. The youngster has made just three substitute appearances in La Liga so far this season and has seen Hansi Flick prefer midfielders Brian Farinas and Frenkie de Jong at full-back at times.

item.title: AEW Full Gear predictions: 5 big questions as Will Ospreay vs. Kyle Fletcher, Anarchy in the Arena await
item.description: AEW Full Gear 2026 , one of the promotion's original pay-per-view franchises, takes place this weekend in Phoenix, Arizona. Featuring at least six championship matches and the annual Anarchy in the Arena brawl, Full Gear looks to continue an impressive 2026 run for Tony Khan's wrestling promotion. With such a loaded card on deck, the Uncrowned Horsemen — Kel Dansby, Robert Jackman, Drake Riggs and Anthony Sulla-Heffinger — are here to break down the event and make predictions for one of the last major AEW events of 2026. Let's ride! 1. Kyle Fletcher and Will Ospreay have a long history together. What's made their rivalry work so well, and where does it go from here? Can it become an all-time AEW rivalry? Jackman: Like other longstanding wrestling partnerships, I think what gives this one the extra oomph is that both men have such a deep personal connection — that they've been friends, as well as opponents and on-off teammates, since the first time they wrestled in front of a crowd, and have since gone on to support each other in making the jump to the big leagues, both in Japan and of course AEW. I mean, they even lived together in Tokyo. When you listen to what we purists call "shoot" interviews, it's clear they have a hell of a lot of trust in each other's abilities. They also both come across as self-critical types who would probably push each other on toward the next level. It's the sort of friendship that will make both men better wrestlers for it. As for what's transpired in AEW, the secret sauce for me has been this long, ongoing thread of the Don Callis Family. You have all the elements of a deep-cut rivalry in there: The fact that Ospreay piggybacked off the Callis Family for a while, only to leave them behind when he decided to be a good guy — whereas Fletcher has stayed in the fold and learned that extra killer instinct from it. It's that same killer instinct that I predict will lead to Fletcher eventually dethroning his real-life bestie — just not this weekend. As for an all-time rivalry, it's basically one rung below Swerve and "Hangman" at the moment. Sulla-Heffinger: The beauty of this rivalry is that their styles and skill set are so similar that it's almost impossible for them not to have excellent chemistry. Nearly every time these two have shared a ring against each other in AEW, it's been in the conversation for Match of the Year. I think from a storytelling standpoint, I equate this to what we've seen play out between Roman Reigns and Seth Rollins in WWE, albeit over a significantly shorter length of time. There are obvious parallels to be made considering Fletcher's closeness with Ospreay in the United Empire and his eventual betrayal of "The Aerial Assassin." With so much history, unmatched skill sets and the fact that both are so young, there's plenty of runway for them to make this the defining men's rivalry of AEW. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) What a difference a month makes. After the Texas Longhorns dropped back-to-back games against Oklahoma and Florida , their hopes for a spot in the College Football Playoff seemed dim. But after three straight wins that include triumphs over ranked teams Ole Miss and Missouri , the No. 6 Longhorns (7-2, 4-2 SEC) enter Saturday's showdown against No. 21 LSU firmly in control of their postseason fate But Texas's first visit to Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La., since 1953 looks tricky. That's not what the rabid Tiger faithful envisioned when the program plucked head coach Lane Kiffin from Ole Miss last season and spent a small fortune on its portal payroll . item.title: This Week in the Minors: Arizona Fall League update
item.description: SCOTTSDALE, AZ - NOVEMBER 08: Zion Rose #8 of the American League fields the ball in the fourth inning during the 2026 Arizona Fall League Fall Stars game between the American League Fall Stars and the National League Fall Stars at Salt River Fields at Talking Stick on Sunday, November 8, 2026 in Scottsdale, Arizona. (Photo by Jill Weisleder/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The Arizona Fall League is an opportunity for prospects to get some extra work in against high-level competition after the minor league season has ended. For some, it’s a chance to make up for lost development time after an injury. For others, it’s an opportunity to get noticed, work on specific parts of their game, or make a strong impression heading into the offseason. The Royals have nine prospects participating this fall, including several familiar names and a few who could be on the radar of more fans in the coming years. Some have put together impressive performances, while others have struggled to find their footing. Let’s take a look at how each of them has performed so far. Felix Arronde The 23-year-old right hander from Cuba has made three starts in the AFL this season. In those three starts, he has totaled 6.1 innings, allowing 3 hits, 3 runs, 2 walks while striking out 8 hitters. Arronde holds a 2-1 record. He is coming off his first year in Northwest Arkansas. This past season he threw 105.1 innings, with a 6.49 ERA. He walked 54 and struck out 91. He had a 1.66 WHIP. He has been with the Royals since he was 18 and coming through the DSL. Josh Hansell Josh Hansell is a 24-year-old right hander. The Royals drafted him in the 16th round in 2023 out of Arizona State. He has never made it past Quad Cities. So far in the AFL, he has made 9 appearances, all out of the bullpen. He has totaled 8.2 innings, allowing 7 hits, 2 runs, walking 6 and striking out 12. His WHIP is at 1.50. This past season in Quad Cities, he made 16 appearances and 6 starts, posting a 4.87 ERA over 40.2 innings. He walked 25 and struck out 41, with a 1.40 WHIP. He missed the last month plus of the season due to injury. Justin Lamkin Justin Lamkin was the most talked about prospect early in the season (at least by me). Before the 22-year-old lefty went down with an injury that cost him the rest of the season, he made eight starts, totaling 39.2 innings, striking out 53 batters between Quad Cities and Northwest Arkansas. He was drafted in the second round of the 2025 draft by the Royals out of Texas A&M. So far in the AFL, he has made five starts, totaling 16.1 innings, allowing 10 hits, 8 runs (7 earned), walking 5 and striking out 14. Dealin' in the desert. @Royals ' No. 8 prospect Justin Lamkin spins 4 1/3 perfect frames in Arizona Fall League play: pic.twitter.com/8dzxOSQq35 — MLB Pipeline (@MLBPipeline) October 22, 2026 I expect him to start next year in Double-A but wouldn’t be surprised if he made a quick jump to Omaha. He is one name to keep an eye on as a prospect

item.title: The Grid Today, Nov. 12: F1 Stands Down Imola, Leaving the Gulf Finale on Schedule
item.description: Floodlights over the Losail circuit in Qatar during a 2010 MotoGP weekend. Illustrative image, not from this year's races. Photo: daly3d abd from Qatar, Doha via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0) With Imola stood down, Formula 1’s 2026 season is still set to finish in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. According to reports from PlanetF1 , The Race and RacingNews365 , F1 told the Italian circuit on Tuesday that it would not be needed as a backup finale. Today’s confirmed news adds one driver announcement: Racing Bulls will keep Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad for 2027. Schedules and announcements below come from formula1.com, the FIA, the circuit organizers and MotoGP’s official site, checked on Nov. 12. Anything that rests on press reports rather than an official statement is labeled that way. The one storyline: Imola is stood down, and the Gulf finale is on Here is what is reported. F1 told Imola it would not host a replacement finale, and informed teams that Qatar (race day Sunday, Nov. 29, at Lusail) and Abu Dhabi (Sunday, Dec. 6, at Yas Marina) stay on the calendar. Imola had been held in reserve for a December 4 to 6 event. PlanetF1 reports that F1 said it could not keep the circuit on standby indefinitely and will cover the costs of the preparations made so far. Here is what is still open. All three outlets paraphrase the decision, and I could not find a full statement on formula1.com, so treat the details as reported. The Race says F1 is reviewing threat assessments “on an hourly basis” and would not hesitate to pull the plug if the risk became unnecessary. RacingNews365 adds that the call is not final and that F1 will act if the situation worsens. On the FIA side, president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said earlier this week that both races will go ahead, as we covered in Tuesday’s briefing . That briefing said F1 had not yet confirmed the finale. These reports, published later the same day, change that picture. The pit lane at Imola during first practice for the 2025 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix. Illustrative image; Imola has now been stood down as a 2026 finale backup. Photo: Jmmuguerza via Wikimedia Commons ( CC BY-SA 4.0 ) Analysis: standing Imola down removes the safety net, and that is the real change. Until now, a cancellation in the Gulf had somewhere to go. From here, any late change would mean a shortened season, not a swap. That raises the stakes on the freight and travel questions we examined in our look at the Gulf finale , and it sits alongside Yamaha’s decision to skip MotoGP Qatar , a reminder that individual teams have already made their own risk calls. Race and session schedule I found no Formula 1, MotoGP or NASCAR track action today. NASCAR finished its season at Homestead on Nov. 8 and the World Endurance Championship at Monza.
