item.title: Satellite snaps rare birds-eye view of the ISS | Space photo of the day for Nov. 12, 2026
item.description: null A satellite looks down at the International Space Station in orbit. (Image credit: HEO) A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station (ISS), giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above. What is it? Most of the time, when we see the ISS, it is from down here on Earth or from the viewpoint of the astronauts onboard, peering out the windows at the station's limbs, solar arrays and instruments. But in this snapshot, which was posted on X on Nov. 9 by the Australian company HEO, we can see the station stretched out in all its glory. HEO specializes in using satellites in low Earth orbit to capture images of other spacecraft, though longer-term the company aims to capture observations far out into the solar system. HEO doesn't build the satellites that take these photos; rather, the company's software tasks the spacecraft to image targets as they come into range. This great photo of the ISS from above, for example, was taken by a satellite operated by BlackSky, a Virginia-based company that holds a non-Earth imaging agreement with HEO . So far, HEO and its partners have captured imagery of a variety of spacecraft in orbit, including the ISS, China's Tiangong space station and the European Space Agency's ERS-2 satellite (while it was hurtling back to Earth in 2024). Why is it incredible? While it might seem that satellites are just hovering above Earth, the space station and other spacecraft in LEO are hurtling through space at roughly 17,500 mph (28,160 kph), hundreds of miles above our planet's surface. A snapshot of a satellite from above is therefore far from mundane. Rather, it requires incredible coordination and technical skill; satellite operators must know precisely when their target will present itself, and their equipment must be capable of getting the shot.

item.title: I used the Vaonis Vespera 3 for weeks and here’s who I would recommend it to — full review
item.description: null I’ve spent a lot of time with smart telescopes , from relatively inexpensive Seestar models to the original Vaonis Vespera and the Vespera Pro . They all promise essentially the same thing — you put a telescope outside at night, choose something interesting on your smartphone and let the technology take care of the rest. The Vaonis Vespera 3 does that exceptionally well, but after spending several nights with it, I’m convinced it’s designed for a rather different kind of buyer. The telescope’s optical arm folds into its curved body when switched off. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) At $2,490/£2,199, this is hardly an impulse purchase for the beginner who’s curious about astronomy – you could buy several perfectly capable smart telescopes for the same money. Yet I found myself increasingly impressed by what the Vespera 3 could achieve, particularly when I returned to the same object over several nights. The images were sharp, the colors were excellent and I almost never had to think about the battery. The Vespera III weighs 13 lbs (6 kg) including the tripod. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) That doesn’t mean the experience was flawless. I sometimes spent longer than I’d have liked waiting for the telescope to get ready, but once it began photographing the sky, the Vespera 3 reminded me why I love smart telescopes so much. Why I kept returning to the same objects over several nights The Vespera 3 uses a Sony IMX585 sensor to produce 8.3MP images. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) One of my favorite things about smart telescopes is watching a photograph develop as more light is collected. What begins as a fairly ordinary patch of stars gradually becomes something much more interesting. First a faint cloud of gas appears, then more structure emerges, and eventually you have an image that, only a few short years ago, would have been difficult to capture without specialist equipment. With the Vespera 3, I spent several nights photographing the Pleiades (M45), the famous star cluster in Taurus. The Pleiades make an excellent subject for testing a telescope because the stars are bright, but the surrounding nebulosity is much harder to capture convincingly. The Singularity app used to control Vespera 3 stacks each image as it goes, but keeps them in sight as an optional time-lapse, so you can see exactly why you’re spending so much time on one object. Even better, the Vespera 3’s PerseverENS feature lets you add data to an existing observation over multiple nights (it’s actually called multi-night observation in the app). Instead of having to call it a night or start again every time the weather interrupts an imaging session, you can return to a target and continue building the image over weeks — or years. This is excellent for faint nebulas, but also for anyone who lives somewhere with unpredictable weather. The Vespera 3 also has CovalENS, Vaonis’s mosaic imaging system, which captures adjacent sections of sky to produce a larger image. That’s helpful for obj

item.title: INEOS' reason for firing Michael Carrick emerges as Manchester United pursue Mauricio Pochettino
item.description: Manchester United fired Michael Carrick on Thursday -Credit:Carl Recine, Getty Images Manchester United have fired Michael Carrick after the club concluded that the players at his disposal are significantly better than what their current Premier League standing reflects. Carrick narrowly kept his position following heavy defeats to Como and AFC Bournemouth two weeks ago and was handed three games to demonstrate he was capable of turning the team's fortunes around. However, United fell to a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge, and although they defeated AS Roma 3-2 and drew 4-4 with Aston Villa, the deficiencies within his squad remained apparent, and the club felt compelled to act during the international break. Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac address Wrexham executive’s abrupt exit Cristiano Ronaldo teases new career venture in social media post after Portugal retirement -Credit:Robin Alam/ISI Photos, ISI Photos via Getty Images United's board felt they had not witnessed enough across those three fixtures to persuade them the team was heading in the right direction. One win from 10 Premier League games has been regarded internally as "not acceptable", as per the Manchester Evening News . INEOS believe United's playing squad is far superior to what their performances and results have demonstrated so far this season, and there is optimism that the change in management will pave the way for a more promising future. Carrick's dismissal was drawn out throughout the week as the club progressed in negotiations to hire Mauricio Pochettino. United maintain they have followed "due process"; however, the manner in which the sacking was handled drew considerable criticism. Carrick continued to oversee training throughout the week, and sources within United have commended him for carrying himself with the utmost professionalism throughout the ordeal. Carrick was originally brought in on a temporary basis in January to replace Ruben Amorim. The Portuguese departed with United sitting in sixth place, and Carrick secured victories in his opening two matches against Manchester City and Arsenal before steering the club to a third-place finish in the division. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE The 45-year-old clinched UEFA Champions League qualification with three matches remaining and was appointed permanently, penning a two-year deal. During the summer transfer window, United brought in Karl Darlow, Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba, investing £150 million (around $200 million) in a midfield overhaul but opting against reinforcing other positions in the squad. Carrick's sole victories this campaign came against newly promoted Ipswich Town, Sabah and Roma. United exited the Carabao Cup against Brighton and Hove Albion, relinquishing a two-goal lead at Old Trafford, but alarm bells rang louder when they suffered a 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League and then a 3-0 loss to Bournemouth days afterward. item.title: How healthy is Kansas football’s quarterbacks room right now?
item.description: LAWRENCE — Last week, before a game at home against UCF, the initial Big 12 Conference player availability report included each of Kansas football’s three leading quarterbacks. Redshirt sophomore Isaiah Marshall, redshirt junior Cole Ballard, and redshirt junior Chase Jenkins were all listed as questionable. By game day, of the three, only Ballard still had some level of status — a game-time decision. And Marshall started, as he has for most of the season, as the Jayhawks (3-6, 1-5 in Big 12) would go on to lose 33-32 against UCF. This week, ahead of a road game Saturday at West Virginia, the initial availability report Wednesday night included just one of those three quarterbacks — Ballard, as questionable. For a KU team that’s in need of a win this weekend, that there’s far less uncertainty at the position is a welcome development. And earlier in the week, coach Lance Leipold signaled as much would be the case. RELATED: Kansas suffers potentially demoralizing loss in defeat against UCF “The health of the quarterback room, as of last night, is probably as good as it’s been in three weeks or so,” Leipold said Monday, before going into an explanation of why the three quarterbacks were questionable initially last week. “As you know, at TCU, Isaiah was a game-time decision, was going to be more of an emergency. So, he was still working through it. So, that’s where he was still continuing in his labeling for the injury report. Cole had taken some hits late in the game and was very limited in practice and was probably more toward the doubtful side and he was probably going to be more emergency this last week. And then Chase missed a day with illness, and did not — and was not in the building, and was extremely limited when he came back. So, that’s why they all were put into that category.” West Virginia (5-4, 2-4) has an offense that’s capable of putting up a lot of points, and a defense that’s allowed a bunch at times this fall. Kansas , too, has encountered its own issues with consistency this year, that have kept it from enjoying the season it came into fall thinking it was capable of. KU needs both Marshall to remain healthy, and for him and the offense as a whole to be able to play at that consistent level this weekend — especially if the Jayhawks’ defense struggles. Marshall’s dual-threat capabilities showed up in the loss against UCF, but Kansas’ success offensively largely came in the second half. With the margin for error getting to where it is now this season for the Jayhawks, they’ll need consistency across all four quarters from all phases. Not just against West Virginia, but in the weeks that follow at home against No. 12 BYU and on the road against Oklahoma State. Jordan Guskey covers University of Kansas Athletics at The Topeka Capital-Journal. He was the 2022 National Sports Media Association’s sportswriter of the year for the state of Kansas. Contact him at JMGuskey@usatodayco.com or on Twitter at @JordanGuskey. This article originall

item.title: Carrick the fall guy for deeper problems at Man Utd – Report
item.description: Michael Carrick is the latest in a long line of managers to be sacked by Manchester United as they struggle to recapture former glories, but their problems run far deeper than the dugout. For the first time in 40 years, the 20-time English champions find themselves in the Premier League relegation zone at this stage of the season. Carrick was handed the job on a permanent basis fewer than six months ago after revitalising the team following the acrimonious departure of Ruben Amorim in January. Under the 45-year-old, then operating as interim boss, United finished third in the Premier League, securing a return to the Champions League after two seasons away. But the optimism quickly vanished at the start of this season and for the third consecutive campaign, woeful results have forced United into a mid-season managerial change. The Red Devils have won just three of their opening 15 games in all competitions. Carrick joins David Moyes, Louis van Gaal, Jose Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag and Amorim among the managers who have struggled to arrest United’s overall decline, despite the occasional trophy, since Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. The Scot stepped down after collecting his 13th Premier League winner’s medal, at the end of a period of dominance in English football and European success. Now United, almost unbelievably, find themselves in a battle just to stay in the English top flight, where they have been ever-present for more than 50 years. USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino — the hot favourite to replace Carrick — faces the task of uniting a deeply divided club on and off the pitch. United captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped last month after he criticised Carrick’s tactics following a 4-1 humbling by Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez took a public swipe at the United hierarchy for not doing more to strengthen the squad in the summer transfer window. Carrick’s role as a player in the glory days under Ferguson meant he retained support among the fanbase despite a string of substandard displays. – Blame game – The anger of the supporters is instead firmly directed towards the club’s owners, whom they hold responsible for overseeing United’s slide. Despite fierce and persistent protests over two decades, the US-based Glazer family still hold a majority stake in the club, which Malcolm Glazer bought via a leveraged takeover in 2005, saddling United with huge debts. Any hopes that the arrival of British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as a minority owner in 2024 would signal a new dawn have since faded. Ratcliffe, founder and chairman of industrial giant INEOS, has overseen cost-cutting measures, including widespread redundancies, and hiked up ticket prices, but the club’s debt has still soared above £1.1 billion ($1.46 billion). Former United captain Gary Neville has lamented the “inept” ownership and leadership of his boyhood club. The Manchester United Supporters’ Trust (MUST), meanwhile, issued a statement following Carrick’s dismiss

item.title: Full-back Barrett leads New Zealand for first time
item.description: Beauden Barrett was part of the 2015 New Zealand World Cup-winning side [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Full-back Beauden Barrett will captain New Zealand for the first time when he leads out the All Blacks for the Nations Championship game against Wales in Cardiff on Saturday. All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has made eight starting changes from the side that defeated Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield with 10 alterations in the match-day 23. It will be 35-year-old Barrett's first time as starting skipper in his 149th international with brother Scott also named at lock, while Richie Mo'unga is at fly-half. "Beauden brings such valuable experience and is massively respected by us all," said Rennie. "Captaining the All Blacks in a Test is an honour I know he doesn't take lightly, so it'll be a proud day for him and his whanau [family]." Basham starts for Wales as Wainwright ruled out Why Wales have a lot to prove despite beating Japan Smiling Rees-Zammit has no fear of All Blacks No Jordan for All Blacks in Cardiff The All Blacks defeated Scotland 43-21 last Saturday, but record try-scoring wing Will Jordan (hamstring) and centre Jordie Barratt (facial) picked up injuries and are absent against Wales. Flanker Anton Segner and wing Fehi Fineanganofo, whose move to Newcastle Red Bulls in the summer was delayed by a year, make their first Test starts. Segner, prop George Bower, hooker Asafo Aumua and scrum-half Cortez Ratima move from the replacements into the starting side. Mo'unga, Fineanganofo, lock Josh Lord and centre Anton Lienert-Brown also come into the side. "We have created good depth in this group and there is a lot of competition for places," said Rennie. "We have selected a strong squad with 783 caps." New Zealand have won the past 34 Tests against Wales in a winning sequence that stretches back to 1953. "Wales are a proud rugby nation and building nicely under Steve Tandy," said Rennie. "We are well aware of the threat they pose and the challenge of playing in front of a passionate crowd at Principality Stadium." New Zealand and South African are currently unbeaten in the southern hemisphere table. The rivals are battling for top spot before the play-off weekend at the end of the month. New Zealand team to face Wales New Zealand: B Barrett (capt); Fineanganofo, Tupaea, Lienert-Brown, Moorby; Mo'unga, Ratima; Bower, Aumua, Newell, S Barrett, Lord, Segner, Lakai, Sititi. Replacements: Bell, Numia, Tosi, Hannah, E Blackadder, Fainga'anuku, Preston, R Ioane.

item.title: Olamide’s Time & Space Is Almost Here! See the Cover Art & 10 Track List
item.description: Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram If Olamide ‘s ‘ Burukutu ‘ has been on repeat, here’s something else to get into: the rapper has revealed the cover art and full tracklist for his upcoming album, Time & Space . Scheduled for release on November 16, 2026, under YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, the ten-track body of work follows a remarkable lineage of musical evolution from one of Africa’s most enduring creative forces. Adding a deeply personal touch to the rollout, Olamide revealed that he personally painted the striking cover art for the project. Olamide hand-painted the official artwork for his upcoming Time & Space, released via YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram Listeners have already caught an exciting glimpse of what to expect from the record through the release of the lead single, Burukutu . Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage, the track serves up rich street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, anchored by rhythmic cadences and unmistakable Yoruba-inflected delivery. The musical journey of Time & Space spans ten carefully curated titles designed to showcase his artistic range. The newly revealed tracklist opens with “ Elohim ” as the introductory piece, followed sequentially by “ Skoskola “, “ Say Less “, the lead anthem “ Burukutu “, and “ Alujon ” rounding out the first half. The second half picks up the tempo with “ Mbiri “, the collaborative track “ Jaiye ” featuring vocalist Fola , followed by “ Oshey “, “ Ring “, and the closing record “ Jogor “. Keeping features remarkably streamlined, the album highlights a targeted guest appearance from Nigerian singer Fola, allowing Olamide’s distinctive penmanship and vocal direction to take centre stage across the entire tracklist. The official 10-track tracklist for Olamide’s album Time & Space, featuring lead single Burukutu and a guest appearance by Fola. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram This forthcoming release arrives as the direct successor to his self-titled studio album, Olamidé , which dropped in June 2025 with a sprawling 17-track setup featuring heavyweights like Wizkid . Where that previous body of work leaned into massive collaborative constellations, Time & Space scales back into a more intimate, focused exploration of sound, anchored tightly by the creative vision of the YBNL boss himself. As November 16 approaches, anticipation continues to build across Lagos and beyond, cementing yet another brilliant chapter in Olamide’s legendary catalogue. item.title: The Beatz Awards Unveils 2026 Nominees, Marking 11 Years Of Celebrating The Creators Behind The Sound
item.description: The Beatz Awards has announced the nominees for its 11th Edition, celebrating 11 years of recognising the creative minds, technical professionals and business stakeholders whose work drives Nigeria’s music industry and the wider African music ecosystem. Guided by the theme “ Behind the Beat, Beyond the Beat ”, this year’s nominations span music production, songwriting, sound engineering, music video direction, broadcasting, digital music platforms, artist management and the wider business of music. The awards spotlight the people and teams whose contributions often happen beyond the public gaze but remain essential to the creation, distribution and commercial success of music. The production categories feature leading and emerging talents across Afro Pop, Afro Beat, Afro R&B, Afro Hip-Hop, Afro Highlife, Afro Soul, Afro Dancehall and Afro Gospel. Nominees include Magicsticks, Sarz, Niphkeys, Ozedikus, Fresh VDM, Ragee, Saszy Afroshii, Tems, Dunnie, Bloody Civilian and rising producers Hunkie Beats, Juixce, Decs, Lekaa Beats, JJAY, Jhay2unez and Shallythechampion. The 2026 field also recognises technical and creative excellence in mixing and mastering, music video direction and songwriting. Broadcasting, media and music business categories include radio and television stations, OAPs, DJs, artist managers, record labels, blogs, online music platforms, A&Rs, live bands and entertainment lawyers. “ Behind every hit record is a team the audience never sees. Our nominees are the engine of African music.” — Elijah John , Founder & Executive Producer, The Beatz Awards Public voting opens on 21 October and runs until 16 November 2026. Music fans and supporters are encouraged to visit the official website, explore the nominees and cast their votes. item.title: Yankees' Cam Schlittler Flexes Cy Young Award Win With One-Word Message
item.description: New York Yankees pitcher Cam Schlittler On Wednesday night, New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler won the American League Cy Young Award. Not only did he win the award, but he won it in unanimous fashion. Schlittler took home all 30 first-place votes. Dylan Cease of the Toronto Blue Jays tallied 22 second-place votes, but the race was not even remotely close. Schlittler was the best pitcher in the American League by far, and he boasted about his victory on X with a one-word post. "Unanimous," Schlittler wrote . That's it. One word to describe a season of excellence for the new Yankees ace. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Schlittler made 14 starts for the Yankees last year, and it was quickly evident that he had the potential to be a special player. He was dominant in the postseason as a rookie as well, going eight scoreless innings with 12 strikeouts in a win-or-go-home Game 3 against the Boston Red Sox in the American League Wild Card Series. For as good as he was last year, he was that much better this year. He had a 1.95 ERA in 33 starts and notched 239 strikeouts. He led the American League in ERA and fWAR. Schlittler was more than deserving of the honor, but now he will have to replicate his success in 2027. The Yankees are trying to win a World Series, and they have too many stars to keep coming up short. For years, Gerrit Cole served as the team's ace, and now it's Schlittler's time to lead the Yankees rotation. More MLB: Insider: Braves' Jurickson Profar 'Certainly Wouldn’t Be Welcome Back'

item.title: Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 enter their 'permanently vulnerable' era
item.description: Microsoft has warned customers still clinging to Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 to consider the software "permanently vulnerable" as November's security fixes arrive for Subscription Edition (SE) alone. The warning appears in the release documentation for November's Exchange Server SE security update. Looking for Exchange 2016 and 2019 information? Tough. Microsoft stated: "Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 are no longer tested for vulnerabilities and there are no updates released. If you are using those versions of Exchange, you should consider them permanently vulnerable [Microsoft's emphasis] and should upgrade your organization immediately." You have been warned. Support for Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 ended on October 14, 2025, but the company announced an Extended Security Updates (ESU) program in July 2025. The plan was that this program would end on April 14, 2026, by which time customers would surely have made the jump to a later or online version, right? The company said: "This period will not be extended past April 2026 (you do not need to ask)." And... of course it was. As April 2026 rolled around, and it became clear that some customers were still stubbornly sticking with the old versions, Microsoft did the equivalent of heaving an exasperated sigh and offered another six months of paid security updates. Those final weeks also brought a separate treat: a Windows Server update breaking Exchange Server . This time it was serious. Microsoft released the final Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 security updates on October 13. No more patches, no more vulnerability testing, and apparently no more reprieves. According to Microsoft's Security Update Guide , the November update fixed nine vulnerabilities in Exchange Server SE, including a critical remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-118207. Microsoft isn't testing earlier versions of Exchange for the vulnerabilities. ®

item.title: Rumble (RUM) Sells Two-Thirds of Its Bitcoin as AI Cloud Business Delivers First Profitable Quarter
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Rumble (RUM) Sells Two-Thirds of Its Bitcoin as AI Cloud Business Delivers First Profitable Quarter RUM Group, the parent of video platform Rumble, cut its bitcoin holdings by about two-thirds in the third quarter, the company disclosed Wednesday, as its newly acquired AI cloud business pushed it to its first profitable quarter on an adjusted basis. The Nasdaq-listed company held 94.68 bitcoin, valued at $7.9 million, as of Sept. 30. That compares with 293.14 bitcoin worth about $17.2 million at the end of June, according to its second-quarter results . That implies Rumble parted with roughly 198 bitcoin during the quarter, or about 68% of its stack. The company’s cash-flow statement shows a net sale of digital assets of about $15.3 million for the first nine months of 2026. In the same period a year earlier, it spent $19.1 million buying digital assets. Rumble did not explain the sales in its release, and it did not say what price it received. The balance sheet’s digital assets line, which the release does not break down, fell to $11.1 million from $18.5 million at the end of 2025. Rumble’s AI pivot takes over The bitcoin drawdown came in a quarter dominated by Quake AI, the cloud and AI infrastructure unit Rumble built around Northern Data, the German GPU operator it acquired in June. Revenue rose 290% from a year earlier to a record $96.6 million, beating the top of the company’s guidance range. Quake AI contributed $68.2 million of that, more than 70% of the total, in its first full quarter. The unit runs about 22,000 Nvidia GPUs, which the company said were about 85% utilized. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $4.4 million, the first positive result in company history. On a GAAP basis, RUM Group still lost $89.9 million, weighed down by $85.2 million in amortization and depreciation. Executives said on the call that about $39 million of that came from writing up the value of Northern Data’s assets in purchase accounting. “Quake AI is now the engine of our business,” CEO Chris Pavlovski said. “We have real assets running real AI workloads for real customers and generating real cash.” The video business itself grew more slowly. Rumble’s video segment brought in $28.4 million, up 15% year over year, and posted a $12.1 million adjusted EBITDA loss, wider than a year earlier, executives said on the call. Cash has been falling as well. RUM Group ended September with $134.4 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $203.3 million at the end of June and $237.9 million at the end of 2025. The company raised its stake in Northern Data to about 98% during the quarter and expects to own all of it in early 2027. It also warned that part of the roughly 250 megawatts of unmonetized capacity it had targeted for 2027 may slip beyond that year due to market conditions. item.title: Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
item.description: Smartglasses have always faced an uphill road to acceptance. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days . Now, Google is ready to take another swing at " intelligent eyewear " for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they're no impulse buy. These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered. Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn't told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea. Read full article Comments

item.title: Reps move to establish national research, innovation fund
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has moved to establish a National Research and Innovation Development Fund to address funding gaps, strengthen Nigeria’s research capacity and promote the commercialisation of locally developed innovations. The proposed legislation also seeks to establish a National Council on Research and Innovation to provide a legal and institutional framework for coordinating research activities, supporting scientific discoveries and transforming research outcomes into marketable products and services. Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, disclosed this on Thursday at a public hearing organised by the House Committee on Science and Technology on the National Research and Innovation Development Fund and National Council on Research and Innovation Bill, 2026 (HB. 2821), at the National Assembly, Abuja. Represented by the Deputy House Leader, Abubakar Halims, Abbas said Nigeria could no longer afford to depend excessively on imported technologies and solutions to challenges its citizens had the intellectual capacity to address. He noted that despite the country’s considerable intellectual resources, talented researchers, innovative young people and skilled entrepreneurs, the absence of an effective system linking research to funding and industry had continued to limit the economic benefits of these capabilities. According to him, research activities in Nigeria often end with academic publications, while promising innovations struggle to attract financing and discoveries with commercial potential fail to progress beyond the laboratory. “The challenge, therefore, is not simply to produce more research, but to build an ecosystem that connects research to funding, innovation to investment, and discoveries to industry,” the Speaker said. He added that the objective of the public hearing was not merely to defend the Bill in its current form but to ensure that the proposed legislation could effectively achieve its intended purpose. Earlier, Chairman of the House Committee on Science and Technology, Zakariya Tijjani Zannah, said Nigeria possessed the human resources and intellectual capacity to drive research and innovation but lacked a dependable legal and institutional framework to finance, coordinate and commercialise research findings. He explained that the proposed legislation was designed to bridge the gap between laboratory discoveries and their practical application in the marketplace. Zannah urged stakeholders to critically examine five major areas of the Bill, including governance and institutional structure, funding sources, grant administration and commercialisation, accountability, and potential implementation gaps. On funding, he drew attention to the proposed 20 per cent contribution from the Nigerian Content Development Fund under Section 19 of the Bill, alongside government appropriations, grants and income generated from commercialisation. item.title: NSCDC orders trial of officer over shooting of trailer driver in Gombe
item.description: ….Commandant relieves personnel of duty, orders disciplinary investigation By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Gombe State Command, has ordered an Orderly Room Trial of a personnel attached to its Anti-Vandal Unit over an alleged shooting incident involving a trailer driver along Gombe Bypass. The incident occurred on Thursday morning, November 12, 2026, at New Mile 3, during a routine enforcement operation by personnel of the unit. The State Commandant, Commandant Muhammed Inuwa Usman, gave the directive following an altercation reportedly involving the NSCDC personnel and the trailer driver, which left the driver with gunshot injuries. In response, Usman ordered the arrest of the officer allegedly involved and relieved him of his operational duties pending the conclusion of disciplinary proceedings. He also constituted a Disciplinary Committee to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that the matter was handled thoroughly, professionally and in accordance with established procedures. The Command disclosed in a statement that the outcome of the Orderly Room Trial and the internal disciplinary process would be made public upon their conclusion. Expressing regret over the incident, Usman reaffirmed the Corps’ commitment to protecting lives and property, upholding professional standards and respecting the fundamental rights of citizens. He stressed that the Command would neither condone nor shield any personnel whose conduct endangered public safety or violated operational guidelines and established rules of engagement. The Commandant appealed to residents, motorists and other members of the public, particularly those around the Gombe Bypass, to remain calm and law-abiding while investigations continued. He also wished the injured driver a speedy recovery, assuring the public that appropriate disciplinary measures would be taken and justice pursued in accordance with the law. The post NSCDC orders trial of officer over shooting of trailer driver in Gombe appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG moves to abolish 269 obsolete laws as review committee submits report
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA– The Federal Government on Thursday began the process of repealing 269 laws it described as obsolete. The action followed the formal presentation of the report of the committee set up in 2024 to review all the laws in the country to the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN. The Committee, which was led by a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) and former Attorney General of Ekiti State, Mr. Olawale Fapohunda, was co-chaired by Professor Dakas Dakas, SAN. While presenting the report to the AGF at the Ministry of Justice headquarters in Abuja, Mr. Fapohunda, SAN, disclosed that the Committee considered a total of 932 federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations. He added that, of the laws considered, 663, together with their relevant subsidiary legislations, were identified for inclusion in the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN), while 269 were found to be obsolete, spent or repealed. Fapohunda, SAN, who noted that significant portions of laws in the country had not undergone a comprehensive, systemic review in nearly two decades, said the revised laws contained in the report of the committee will usher in a forward-looking era for Law Reform in Nigeria. “Our primary objective was clear—to purge obsolete and redundant statutes, resolve conflicting provisions, and seamlessly integrate contemporary socio-economic and technological realities into our national legal framework. “The statutory laws of any nation are the bedrock of its governance, economic stability, and social justice. However, a legal system that remains stagnant while society evolves becomes an impediment to progress. “Our Committee was confronted with laws that still referenced obsolete economic indicators, archaic penalties, and administrative frameworks that do not align with modern technological advancements or international best practices. “Our mandate was not merely to edit, but to fundamentally sanitize our statute books. “In carrying out this responsibility, the Committee took care to preserve the substance of existing laws and to distinguish between legislation that remained in force, legislation that had been repealed, legislation that had become spent, and legislation requiring further legislative attention. “To ensure a thorough and inclusive outcome, the Committee adopted a multi-layered approach: Fourteen Working Groups were constituted to undertake the detailed review of the assigned volumes of legislation, supported by Technical Teams responsible for collation, drafting, quality assurance, oversight and editorial review. “This structure was designed to ensure that the review was undertaken systematically, while providing successive levels of technical and editorial scrutiny. Particular attention was given to the need for accuracy and consistency,” the Committee Chairman added. He expressed the hope that the exercise will lay the foundation of a more regular and sustainable system of law

item.title: Ghana launches smaller, tougher banknotes to fight counterfeiting
item.description: Ghana unveiled smaller, longer-lasting banknotes on Thursday, introducing upgraded anti-counterfeiting safeguards and designs celebrating its national heritage as it modernises its currency. The central bank said the redesign was necessary because some core banknote designs have been in circulation for more than two decades, while counterfeiting technology and international security standards have evolved. Made from reinforced cotton paper, the new notes are designed to withstand frequent handling and Ghana’s tropical climate, reducing wear and the cost of replacing damaged currency. Improved tactile markings will also help people with visual impairments distinguish between notes, the bank said. They are also portable, moving towards the compact banknote formats familiar in Europe and other international markets. “The new notes are also smaller and easier to handle,” President John Mahama said at an an event where the notes were launched, describing the improvements as practical changes for everyday transactions. The so-called “Heritage Series” will enter circulation on December 1 alongside existing notes, which remain legal tender, Bank of Ghana Governor Johnson Asiama said at a ceremony in Accra. The overhaul retains eight denominations, ranging from one to 200 cedis, including the return of the two-cedi banknote. It does not change the currency’s value or amount to a redenomination. Beyond security, the new designs celebrate Ghanaian national heroes including former UN secretary-general Kofi Annan and the country’s first president Kwame Nkrumah, historic landmarks and monuments. Ghana introduced the cedi as its national currency in July 1965, eight years after gaining independence from Britain. The redesign comes as the West African nation expands digital payments, although the central bank insisted physical currency remained indispensable. “Physical cash remains an essential pillar of our monetary resilience,” Asiama said, warning that cyberattacks, technical failures and natural disasters could disrupt electronic payment networks. The central bank is also preparing legislation to replace the 1964 currency act, strengthening provisions against counterfeiting and the deliberate destruction or misuse of banknotes. The post Ghana launches smaller, tougher banknotes to fight counterfeiting appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: France's social safety net: Can it afford to be so generous?
item.description: Created in the aftermath of World War II, France's social security system has become one of the pillars of French society, providing everything from healthcare and family benefits to pensions. But with an ageing population and mounting deficits, this ambitious model is facing a major financial test. We look at how the system works, why it is so deeply valued by the French and whether the country can afford to keep its promise of protecting everyone – from cradle to grave.

item.title: BlackRock’s IBIT Bleeds $2 Billion in Nine Straight Days of Outflows
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine BlackRock’s IBIT Bleeds $2 Billion in Nine Straight Days of Outflows BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost another $269.7 million on Wednesday, its ninth straight session of redemptions, as U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds posted a fifth consecutive day of net outflows totaling $299.8 million. Across the nine sessions since Oct. 30, IBIT has shed about $2 billion. The fund, the largest of the U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs, has seen money leave on every trading day so far in November. The broader group has fared only slightly better. The 11 funds have lost about $1.44 billion over the past five trading days and roughly $1.88 billion in November, with outflows on seven of the month’s eight sessions. The lone exception was Nov. 4, when $74.6 million came in, even as IBIT itself bled $201.2 million that day. IBIT accounts for about $1.77 billion of November’s outflows, or roughly 94% of the total. Wednesday’s selling was concentrated. Besides IBIT, Grayscale’s GBTC lost $39.1 million, while Morgan Stanley’s MSBT was the only fund to take in money, about $9 million. The rest of the funds reported no flows. IBIT streak still short of this year’s worst The current run is not a record. Both the group and IBIT went 13 straight trading days without an inflow from May 15 to June 3, the longest outflow streaks of 2026. IBIT followed that with an 11-session streak from June 17 to July 2. Still, the size of the recent withdrawals stands out. IBIT’s two largest daily outflows of the year both came this month: $405.3 million on Nov. 2 and $403 million on Nov. 6. The selling has also flipped the year. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs are now down about $1.42 billion in net flows for 2026, compared with roughly $25.2 billion of inflows at the same point last year. The Australian Financial Review noted Thursday that the selling has erased this year’s net inflows into the funds. IBIT is still positive for the year, with about $2.45 billion in net inflows in 2026 and roughly $64.5 billion since it launched in January 2024. That cushion has shrunk quickly. IBIT took in about $932 million in October, and November’s withdrawals have already erased that amount nearly twice over. The withdrawals come just days after BlackRock argued that security fears were driving bitcoin whales out of self-custody and into IBIT. Why bitcoin ETF investors are pulling back The outflows began before this week’s worst headlines but have picked up alongside them. A hotter-than-expected October inflation report on Tuesday lifted bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, and Polymarket odds of a hike climbed to about 97%, Yahoo Finance reported . Higher rates make cash and bonds more attractive relative to assets like bitcoin. Tech stocks have added pressure. Nvidia shares fell roughly 9% after Wednesday’s close following reports that its board was preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang, and Nasdaq 100 futures slid with them. item.title: Bitcoin Price Falls Below $72,000 as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Steps Down and Strategy (MSTR) Slides
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls Below $72,000 as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Steps Down and Strategy (MSTR) Slides Bitcoin price fell below $72,000 on Thursday morning, its lowest level since mid-August, after Nvidia said CEO Jensen Huang had resigned and Strategy shares slid following MSCI’s confirmation of an index exit, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The selling started after Wednesday’s close. Bitcoin slipped from about $74,700 to near $73,400 by 6 p.m. ET, then drifted sideways overnight. A second leg lower began around 6 a.m., and the bitcoin price briefly dipped to about $72,200 shortly after 8 a.m. The decline accelerated later in the morning, and bitcoin traded as low as about $71,670 around 9:29 a.m. That move pushed the bitcoin price below the low near $72,700 it set after Tuesday’s hotter-than-expected inflation report . It now trades roughly $31,200 below where it stood one year ago. Nvidia CEO steps down, and the bitcoin price follows Nvidia (NVDA) said Thursday that Huang has resigned as president, chief executive and a member of the board, effective immediately. The company named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO and appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first board chair. Kress will continue as chief financial officer while she serves in the interim role. The board is searching for a permanent successor and said it will consider internal and external candidates. Nvidia is still scheduled to report fiscal third-quarter results on Nov. 17. The resignation follows reports of extramarital relationships, including one that has raised national security concerns in Washington. Sen. Kevin Cramer, a North Dakota Republican, had told CNBC that Huang should step down, saying he was “so vulnerable to extortion, blackmail.” Nvidia shares fell about 13% at Thursday’s open. Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 1.4% and S&P 500 futures fell about 0.7%, while Dow futures were nearly flat. Intel, Marvell Technology and Micron were down between about 5% and 7.5%, and CoreWeave dropped about 16%, giving back most of Wednesday’s 24.7% surge. Data center firms IREN, Applied Digital and Core Scientific also traded lower. Bitcoin price has moved with tech for most of this month. It fell on Monday when an earlier Nvidia probe rattled markets, then lagged Wednesday’s rebound in chip stocks. Thursday’s slide wiped out that small gain and then some. Strategy slides after MSCI confirms index exit Strategy (MSTR), the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, fell about 7% at the open after MSCI confirmed it will remove the stock from its indexes. MSCI’s November review removed Strategy from the MSCI USA Index , a step that also takes it out of the MSCI World and ACWI indexes, effective at the Nov. 30 close. Japan’s Metaplanet is also slated for removal. Index funds will sell MSTR shares, not bitcoin, and nothing in the rules requires Strategy to sell its coins. item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive
item.description: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of the company, following the revelation of his affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy and reports of a relationhip another woman who was a company employee. In a Form 8-K [PDF] filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the GPU maker disclosed that it accepted the resignation of Huang, whom it identified as Jen-Hsun Huang, on November 11, effective immediately. He is being replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim leader while the board conducts a search for a new CEO. Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as president, CEO, and a member of the board of directors ever since, led the GPU maker to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, hitting a hit peak of over $5.5 trillion earlier this year. His position became untenable following an investigation by the company's board after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a romantic relationship with a woman the US authorities suspected as a Chinese spy. Reports later surfaced this week of a second alleged affair with an employee of the company itself, reported by the New York Times as being with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. This is a developing story which will be expanded as more detail emerges. ®

item.title: Court fixes Friday for judgment in PDP, Adebutu’s suit against INEC
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja fixed Friday to deliver judgment in a suit filed by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) seeking to compel the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish the name of its candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, for the 2027 Ogun governorship election. Justice Peter Lifu fixed the date after parties called their witnesses and adopted their processes in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/2573/2026. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the PDP and Adebutu had, on Oct. 22, filed the suit following the removal of Adebutu’s name from the list of contestants of the governorship seat in Ogun. The plaintiffs sued INEC as the sole defendant in the suit filed by their lawyer, Ahmed Raji, SAN. The plaintiffs, who sought six questions for determination, prayed the court for 11 reliefs. They sought an order setting aside the commission’s decision to omit, remove or refuse to publish Adebutu’s name in the final list of candidates published on Oct. 10 for denial of a fair hearing and violation of the provisions of Section 29 and Section 32 of the Electoral Act, 2026. They also sought an order directing or compelling “the defendant to, within twenty-four (24) hours of the order/orders of this honourable court, include and/or publish the name of the 2nd plaintiff as the 1st plaintiff’s governorship candidate for Ogun State in the forthcoming 2027 General Election,” among other reliefs. In a counter-affidavit deposed to by Mr Mustapha Mohammed, a Chief Programme Analyst in its Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Department, INEC told the court that Adebutu’s name was not found in the register of members the PDP earlier submitted to it. INEC told the court that it found only the name of the PDP’s deputy governorship candidate in the state, Kolapo Lateefat Oyeyemi, in the register. Meanwhile, at the last sitting on Nov. 5, the plaintiffs and the defendants called their witnesses to testify as to the propriety of their claims. Giving his evidence on behalf of the plaintiffs, the PDP National Organising Secretary, Umar Bature, told the court that in the flash drive submitted to INEC which contained all the names of its candidates, the name of Adebutu was included. Bature, who was led in evidence by Raji, stated that contrary to the colour of the INEC’s flash drive brought to the court, the flash drive submitted to the commission was silver in colour. The PDP witness said the party only submitted a soft copy of the list of their candidates, which was the flash drive, to the electoral umpire in line with the Electoral Act and Paragraph 4(3) of Part 1 of the Regulations and Guidelines for Political Parties, 2026, issued by INEC. In his testimony, Mohammed, the Chief Programme Analyst with INEC, insisted that Adebutu’s name was not in the list of names of candidates submitted to the commission. item.title: [Photos] ‘They came in four buses’ – NDC member narrates how thugs invaded Lagos rally
item.description: *We weren’t informed of political rally – Police By Mathew Johnson It was a terrifying experience for members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, who had gathered for a town hall meeting in Oregun, Lagos, on Thursday. The event was part of the scheduled visit of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and vice, Rabiu Kwankwanso. Read Also: Video: Thugs attack NDC supporters in Lagos According to some of the supporters’ accounts, the gathering was disrupted when about 50 suspected political thugs, allegedly armed with guns, cutlasses, axes, machetes and other dangerous weapons, stormed the premises, attacking party members. The ensuing stampede sent participants scampering for safety. Recounting how the attack unfolded, one of the party members, Olamilekan Olayiwola, Ward F Chairman and security coordinator at the event, said party members had arrived at the venue as early as 8a.m. They then noticed five commercial buses – LT buses – parked outside the premises. According to him: “The incident happened as supporters were waiting for preparations at the hall to be completed ahead of Peter Obi’s arrival. “The attack started around 8a.m. Before it happened, I saw five LT buses parked outside the premises, with their occupants threatening to scatter everything. “They had guns, cutlasses and axes. They attacked us, forcing some of our members to mobilise the women to defend themselves. “Four party members sustained injuries during the clash, while several others lost their mobile phones. There was no police officer on the ground, except for two DSS operatives, who fired warning shots into the air to disperse the attackers. “I am calling on political leaders and security agencies to put adequate security arrangements in place for campaign events and polling units across Lagos State because. “If nothing is done, the situation could turn bloody.” However, at the time of time of writing this report, armed policemen numbering over 20 were sighted at the scene, while members were still waiting for Obi and Kwankwaso’s arrival. item.title: ‘I’m Here’, Fubara Declares As Wike Inaugurates Rainbow Coalition, APC Campaign Council In Rivers
item.description: The Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, on Thursday, declared his unwavering support for the All Progressives Congress (APC), stating that he is fully involved in the Rainbow Coalition movement. He made the declaration as the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, inaugurated members of the Rivers APC Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in the State. He urged members to demonstrate through their actions that they are committed to the political cause ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor said he expected members to be honest about their political convictions, stressing that those unwilling to support his position should openly take a different path rather than engage in double-dealing. He said his political decision is firm and would not be different whether expressed publicly or privately. “Don’t say you’re openly with me, and behind you’re doing a different thing. I’m here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day, in private and in secret. I have taken this position, and anybody who says he is not with me, gently go your way.” Gov. Fubara also urged members to put past political differences behind them, noting that the new campaign council has brought together a broader spectrum of political stakeholders, including some who were previously in opposition. He described the expanded composition of the council as an advantage that could strengthen the coalition’s chances if members worked together. Recalling the 2023 general elections, the governor said a similar political structure had helped secure victory for him and President Bola Tinubu, expressing confidence that the new council could deliver even more votes in 2027. He challenged members to approach the assignment with determination, insisting that electoral success would depend on their willingness to work collectively towards a common objective. “If we take it as a serious responsibility, a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out decisive, with a stronger vote that is more than what we did in 2023.” The governor congratulated members of the inaugurated council and assured those who were not included in the initial list that additional committees would be constituted and the structure could still be expanded. He expressed appreciation to the council’s leadership and other political stakeholders for their efforts, praying for success in the task ahead. The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, speaking while inaugurating members of the Rivers APC Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in Rivers State on Thursday, November 12, 2026. item.title: Huang powers and bankrolls AI revolution: Nvidia CEO caught between 'a rock and a very hard place'
item.description: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of France's Institute of Digital Sovereignty. Benhamou examines the intersection of traditional espionage, geopolitical rivalry and the extraordinary concentration of power within the global AI industry. Discussing allegations surrounding Nvidia's leadership, he describes the chipmaker as "the banker of the global AI system," a striking characterization that captures the company's importance not merely as a semiconductor manufacturer, but as a central actor in the economic and technological infrastructure underpinning the AI boom. "Because humans stay humans." Benhamou identifies one of the central paradoxes of the artificial intelligence revolution: even as technological systems acquire unprecedented strategic and economic importance, the individuals who control them remain susceptible to familiar forms of influence, manipulation and misjudgment.

item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of AI giant Nvidia on Thursday, the company said, after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor, ending Huang’s 33-year run at the helm of the global juggernaut he co-founded. Huang, 63, also gave up his seat on the board. The company did not give a reason for his departure. The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion-dollar company plunging, and the exit of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom, leaves Nvidia without its founding leader at a crucial time for the sector. Nvidia shares were down more than 10 percent in premarket trading Thursday following the announcement. The stock was already down around 25 percent from its all-time high in early October. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. The board said it had appointed Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as its first-ever chair. “The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption,” Jones said in a statement. Kress said she was committed to “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.” – Two affairs – The scandal began with reports that Huang, who has been married to Lori Huang for more than 40 years, was involved in an extramarital relationship. Jensen Huang admitted on Sunday to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, who was a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. On Sunday, Nvidia’s board announced a probe into what it called reporting that Huang had been the target of a “foreign intelligence effort,” while saying it retained confidence in him. On Wednesday, The New York Times reported that Huang had a second extramarital affair, citing video evidence of him being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand its technology into higher education and health care. She was speaking at a conference in San Jose, California, where the two “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. item.title: ‘To them, we’re just NPCs’: the artists and activists challenging Trump’s video game propaganda
item.description: Order a Diet Coke or invade Iran – that’s the choice facing the US president in one of several satirical games, as designers turn the gamification of politics back on the White House In early September, the Trump White House announced a surprising new addition to its official website. Named simply Arcade , it is a collection of browser games based on classic titles such as Flappy Bird, Snake, and Tetris, but re-tuned as flagrant works of political propaganda. Designed to court reactionary gamers, they push the administration’s policies on immigration and other hot-button issues, while dehumanising their targets. There have recently been some new additions: a Temple Run clone named Red Scare about crossing the “ration market” and escaping the Democratic Socialists of America, and another simple item-matching game about the threat of socialism. In the midst of increasing fuel, utility and grocery prices thanks to the Iran war, these were naked attempts to distract voters by appealing to their video game nostalgia. After an explosion of news coverage, Arcade caught the attention of the games industry. The Tetris Company warned on social media that it “took copyright infringement very seriously.” Days later, the game was removed from the White House site. However, aside from a March 2026 statement from the Pokémon Company condemning the White House for using its characters in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) propaganda, major video game companies have been relatively silent in the face of the administration’s widespread usage of their IP. item.title: Vast data dump from Euclid space telescope reveals stunning galaxies
item.description: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The European Space Agency has just released a vast batch of observations of the sky captured by the Euclid space telescope. Launched in 2023, the telescope is currently on a six-year mission to image about one-third of the sky to build the most detailed 3D map of the cosmos ever created . The latest observations – catchily titled DR1-Foundation – cover an area of the sky as big as 9500 full moons. The collection includes 900 million galaxies. The mosaic of 740 images at the top of the article, collected in autumn 2024 and spring 2025, covers 367 square degrees of the northern sky. At full resolution, this snapshot runs to 500 gigapixels. Advertisement The bright oval in the lower left portion of the patchwork image is the spiral galaxy Messier 81, which is some 12 million light years from Earth. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The image above shows Messier 81 in greater detail, along with part of the M81 group of galaxies that also bears its name – an honour bestowed on it as the largest galaxy of the bunch. To the lower left is the smaller galaxy NGC 3077, and the patches of wispy blue cloud throughout the images are galactic cirrus, which are actually in the foreground and part of our own home galaxy. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO Here, Messier 81 is shown in even greater detail, in an image taken at the full resolution available to Euclid. The haze dominating the right side of the frame is the disc of Messier 81, inside which individual stars are visible. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO This hazy galaxy is NGC 1291, around 33 million light years away. The image was made from two taken by Euclid and then cropped. In the background, even more distant galaxies are visible – the furthest away of which show up in red. Stars are still actively forming within NGC 1291, and can be seen as small blue-hued dots. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The image above shows Abell 3128, a cluster of hundreds of galaxies lying around 800 million light years away. The cluster is home to a diverse array of galaxies, including whirling spirals and fuzzy ellipticals. In the centre of the image is a strong gravitational lens, where the light travelling to us from a more distant galaxy has been warped by a massive object in the foreground.

item.title: The 'eclipse of the century' will plunge these 8 wonders of the Roman Empire into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027
item.description: null Ancient Egyptian temples will inevitably dominate the story of the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . After all, the path of totality crosses Luxor, home to Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the ancient world's most famous monuments. But follow the moon 's shadow west and another ancient civilization comes into view. Before reaching Egypt, totality will sweep across the Mediterranean and North Africa, passing over an extraordinary collection of Roman cities, fortresses, theaters, temples and triumphal arches. Many lie within what became Rome's North African provinces, a region that produced some of the empire's wealthiest and most impressive cities. From beachside Baelo Claudia in Spain and military Tamuda in Morocco to Timgad and Djémila in Algeria and the jaw-dropping El Jem Amphitheater in Tunisia, Roman ruins will experience between two and more than five minutes of darkness — creating extraordinary possibilities for eclipse chasers and photographers. Here are some of the best places to watch the moon's shadow cross what was once the Roman Empire. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date . 1. Baelo Claudia, Spain Baelo Claudia's Roman ruins overlook Bolonia beach and the Strait of Gibraltar. (Image credit: Andrea Pucci via Getty Images) Location: near Tarifa, Andalucía, Spain Start of totality and duration: 10:44 a.m. CEST; 4 minutes, 31 seconds Historical cloud cover: 12% Altitude of the sun: 37 degrees above east Roman ruins, an Atlantic beach and the mountains of Africa could all share the frame with the eclipsed sun at Baelo Claudia. Founded in the second century B.C., this remarkably well-preserved Roman city near Bolonia beach includes a forum, basilica, theater, temples, baths and a decumanus maximus (east-west street), all set against forested hills and a vast coastal sand dune. For photographers, the possibilities are exceptional — columns and temples may provide an ancient foreground, while wider compositions could incorporate the beach and dunes. On particularly clear days, Morocco is visible across the Strait of Gibraltar — potentially putting Roman ruins, two continents and a total solar eclipse into one extraordinary scene. 2. Málaga Roman Theatre, Spain The Roman Theatre at the foot of the Málaga Alcazaba dates back to the 1st century BC. (Image credit: Manfred Gottschalk via Getty Images) Location: Málaga, Spain Start of totality and duration: 10:48 a.m. CEST; 1 minute, 57 seconds Historical cloud cover: 9% Altitude of the sun: 39 degrees above east Few eclipse locations can offer two civilizations in the same photograph. Málaga's Roman Theatre was built in the first century B.C., when the city was part of the Roman province of Hispania, and today sits directly beneath the Alcazaba, the imposing Muslim-era palace-fortress that dominates the hillside above. Although its totality is considerably shorter than locations farther south, the photographic possibilities ar

item.title: Trump says US does not ‘need a deal with Iran’
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that he was directing Vice President JD Vance to focus completely on domestic anti-fraud efforts and not negotiations towards a deal to end war with Tehran. “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. His comments came shortly after the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Vance was mulling face-to-face talks with a top Iranian security official. The Journal’s report added Trump had told aides and counterparts that he was open to Vance reopening talks with Tehran, and that the president had empowered Vance to negotiate. Such an in-person meeting would mark an unusual move. Oil prices rose after Trump’s remarks on social media, while Wall Street futures slipped further. Trump’s comments also come after his Republican Party were hit by sweeping losses in this month’s midterm elections, with Democrats gaining control of Congress. Anger over war with Iran, which has caused fuel prices to surge in the United States, has been seen as a key factor pushing voters away from Republicans. Vance was among Republicans to blame the Iran war for the party’s losses at the ballot box. The conflict has been ongoing since US-Israel strikes on Iran from late February, prompting Tehran to choke off the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for energy transit. The blockage has wreaked havoc on the world economy, causing energy costs to rocket. The post Trump says US does not ‘need a deal with Iran’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Trump wrote on Truth Social. item.title: Seyi Tinubu gets Northern youths’ backing over Gwandu title
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja A Northern youth organisation, the Northern Youth Frontiers, Northwest Zone, has commended the conferment of a traditional title on President Bola Tinubu’s son, Seyi Tinubu, by the Emir of Gwandu, Alhaji Muhammadu Iliyasu Bashar. The group described the honour as recognition of Seyi Tinubu’s contributions to youth empowerment, community development and humanitarian activities, urging him to use the recognition as motivation to deepen his commitment to young Nigerians and national unity. Seyi Tinubu was turbaned as Dan Zaki Gwandu, meaning “Son of the Lion of Gwandu”, at the historic Abdullahi Fodiyo Palace in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State. In a congratulatory statement on Thursday, the Northwest Coordinator of the organisation, Saminu Turaki, said the honour reflected what he described as Tinubu’s contributions to youth empowerment, community development and humanitarian services across the country. Turaki described the title, reportedly the first of its kind in the history of the Gwandu Emirate, as more than a ceremonial recognition, saying it underscored the importance of service, leadership and relationships that transcend ethnic and cultural boundaries. He said the development demonstrated the enduring relationship between traditional institutions and efforts to promote national unity, noting that traditional rulers remained important custodians of Nigeria’s cultural heritage and social cohesion. “This historic honour reflects the enduring bonds of friendship, mutual respect and national unity among Nigeria’s diverse peoples, highlighting the critical role traditional institutions play as custodians of our culture and national cohesion,” he said. The group also expressed solidarity with Seyi Tinubu as he assumes the responsibilities associated with the traditional title, expressing confidence that he would uphold the values of courage, humility, leadership and selfless service. “We are confident that he will embody the core values of courage, leadership, humility and selfless service associated with this esteemed title. We encourage him to let this honour further inspire his commitment to empowering young Nigerians and promoting peaceful coexistence,” Turaki said. The organisation urged the new Dan Zaki Gwandu to use the recognition as an opportunity to expand initiatives that create opportunities for young people and promote peaceful coexistence across the country. It also wished him wisdom, strength and divine guidance in discharging the responsibilities associated with the traditional honour and serving humanity and the nation. item.title: Quantum leap: IBM plans to scale beyond 1,000 qubits in 2027 with Nighthawk r3 processor
item.description: IBM has unveiled the Nighthawk r3, an upcoming next-gen quantum processor that will feature 520 qubits, as another step towards a planned fault-tolerant quantum system it hopes to launch in 2029. Big Blue's current Nighthawk r2 was only made available in September and features 120 quantum bits (qubits) capable of handling circuits using 7,500 operations. Its successor, IBM claims, will have more than four times as many qubits and execute 10,000 quantum operations to tackle larger, more complex problems while maintaining the same speed and accuracy. Nighthawk r3 is slated to arrive in 2027, when Big Blue plans to link two of the quantum processors into a single system with more than 1,000 qubits. IBM said applications increasingly require circuits executing thousands of quantum operations on approximately 100 qubits or more, speeding up collection of the millions or billions of samples needed to perform complex computations. Speed determines whether such demanding workloads can be completed in practical timeframes and at a reasonable cost. The new quantum processor will feature 10 chip-to-chip interconnects, called l-couplers, designed for linking together processors that it will use to enable a single 1,040-qubit system. This tech was tested using Nighthawk r1 processors . IBM previously outlined its goal of reaching reliable error correcting territory in 2029 with a quantum processor codenamed Starling. Now it intends for this to be the world’s first fault-tolerant quantum computer , capable of running quantum circuits comprising 100 million quantum operations on 200 logical qubits. This is an ambitious goal, considering fault-tolerant quantum technology always seems to be at least a decade away, despite numerous breakthroughs and technology introductions. However, some in the technology industry believe the odds on a working system are shortening , given the increased activity around making encryption ready with support for quantum-resistant algorithms. Then again, a professor at the University of Auckland New Zealand famously claimed last year that quantum computers hadn't so far managed to factor any number greater than 21 without cheating. IBM presented a framework for Starling in a 2025 paper outlining hardware to implement the improbably named bivariate bicycle quantum low-density parity check (qLDPC) error correction codes. These significantly reduce the number of physical qubits needed to store and process quantum information, compared to existing surface codes. Using the architecture in the paper, Big Blue intends to assemble Starling from modules that each contain a quantum memory and logical processing unit (LPU), allowing logic operations on the memory. The modules will have universal adapters letting them connect using l-couplers. IBM is also preparing the way ahead by combining its quantum processors with classical high-performance compute (HPC) systems to research better quantum error correction. item.title: Migration to developed countries declines for second year – OECD
item.description: Migration to developed countries dwindled for a second year in a row in 2025, down 1.6 percent compared to the previous year, according to an OECD report published Thursday. While still experiencing high numbers, the 38 Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries recorded 6.1 million new permanent immigrants in 2025, compared to 6.2 million the previous year. There has been a backlash in many Western countries against the arrival of irregular migrants fleeing conflict, authoritarian rule and economic hardship in their home countries. Legal humanitarian migration dropped “sharply” by 26 percent in 2025 compared with 2024, the report found. Labour migration increased by 13 percent. While 2025 marked an overall decline in migration, the number of permanent immigrants settling for the long term was up 12 percent compared with 2019. Three countries recorded a notable spike in permanent migrants in 2025. Portugal saw a 139-percent increase to 313,600 individuals, resulting from approvals of a backlog of pending residency permits. Spain saw a 25-percent increase to 460,500 people, notably after having broadened its residency policies. Italy saw a 45-percent increase to 248,800 people, largely attributed to a flux of family and labour migration. Other countries saw significant declines in permanent migrants. The United States saw a 14-percent drop, although it still leads OECD countries, recording more than 1.2 million permanent migrants in 2025. Canada saw a 19-percent decrease to 393,800 people, and the United Kingdom a 32 percent decline to 295,800 people. – Asylum seekers down – India remained the leading country of origin for migratory flows to the OECD in 2024, ahead of China and Colombia, according to the latest available figures. The 1.1 million asylum applications in 2025 marked a 22-percent decrease to OECD countries, excluding the United States, compared with the previous year, although remaining about 10 percent higher than 2019 figures. Men continue to account for the majority of migratory flows to OECD countries. According to the latest available data from 2024, women accounted for about 46 percent of new immigrants. The OECD countries that admitted significantly more women than men were the United States and Ireland with 54 percent female immigrants; Sweden with 53 percent, and Israel, Chile, Australia and New Zealand with 52 percent. Migration poses an opportunity to boost long-term productivity in many countries, particularly in the face of aging populations, the OECD noted. “With the OECD working-age population set to decrease by 8 percent by 2060, pushing overall growth downwards, reviving productivity growth is key to maintaining living standards,” said Mark Pearson, the OECD’s acting director of Employment, Labour and Social Affairs. “Immigrants now account for 16 percent of employment across the OECD, 3 percentage points more than a decade ago,” he added.
